Paul continues: “For this slight momentary affliction is preparing us for an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure, because we look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen; for what can be seen is temporary, but what cannot be seen is eternal.” He calls his sufferings slight and momentary, not because they were small, but because he has placed them on a scale beside the glory that is coming, and the glory is heavier. St John Chrysostom, preaching on this letter, says that Paul makes affliction light by setting it beside the reward, and short by setting it beside eternity (Homilies on 2 Corinthians, in substance). That is true wisdom, the wisdom the name Sophia speaks of: to judge things by their weight in eternity. The house, the land, the results in the examination, the praise of the neighbours, all these can be seen, and all are temporary. Faith, hope and love, the soul of a child, a kindness done in secret, the grace of the Holy Qurbono, these cannot be seen, and they remain. A wise person spends the visible to gain the invisible.

The Gospel tells how to do that. Jesus is near Jerusalem, and his hearers think the kingdom is about to appear at once. So he tells of a nobleman who goes to a distant country to receive royal power and then return. Before leaving he gives ten servants a pound each and says: “Do business with these until I come back.” The time between his going and his return is our time, the time of the Church after the Ascension and Pentecost. When he comes back, one servant has made ten pounds and hears, “Well done, good slave! Because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities.” Another wrapped his pound in a cloth, because he was afraid. The parable ends with hard words about the citizens who said, “We do not want this man to rule over us.” Jesus is not teaching violence; he is going up to Jerusalem to die for those who reject him, and on the Cross he will pray for them. The harsh ending tells us how serious it is to refuse the true King. St Gregory the Great explained that the gift entrusted to each of us is whatever we have received: let the one who has understanding take care not to keep silent, the one who has means not to be slow in mercy, the one who has a skill to share its use (Homilies on the Gospels 9, in substance). The pound is the faith, the gifts of the Spirit and the time given to us. Do not bury it. Trade with it until he comes.
outline: Opening
Ask: what pound has the Lord given me that I have wrapped in a cloth?
Point 1 · Renewed day by day
The outer nature wastes away; the inner person grows young in the Spirit.
Point 2 · What cannot be seen
The wisdom that weighs everything on the scale of eternity.
Point 3 · Do business until I come back
The time of the Church is the time for using the gifts we were given.
Take-home line
“We look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen.”
live: Unwrap one pound (Luke 19:13)
Name one gift you have stopped using for God, a voice, a skill, a little money, some time, and use it once this week for the parish or for someone in need.
Weigh it on the right scale (2 Corinthians 4:18)
Before one decision today, ask: what will this mean in eternity?
2027-05-25.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you went away to receive your kingdom and you will come again in glory. While we wait, you have entrusted to us the gifts of your grace. Renew our inner nature day by day by your Holy Spirit, even when our outer nature grows weak. Give us the true wisdom that looks at what cannot be seen, and keep us from the fear that buries what you have given. With St Sophia and all your saints, let us be found trustworthy in small things, so that at your coming we may hear your word of welcome. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the unseen is given under what is seen: in the Holy Qurbono bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ, the eternal weight of glory hidden in a humble gift.

2027-05-26.title: Wednesday of the first week after Pentecost · St Philip Neri
readings: You accepted it not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word
“Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life”
2027-05-26.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the First Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Philip Neri, priest, founder of the Congregation of the Oratory (died 1595).
2027-05-26.verse: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.
theo: The Gospel today is only three verses long, but it comes at the hinge of St John's sixth chapter. On Sunday we heard Jesus speak of the true bread from heaven. In the verses that follow he says plainly that the bread is his flesh, given for the life of the world, and that whoever eats his flesh and drinks his blood has eternal life. Many disciples find this too hard and walk away. Then Jesus turns to the Twelve: “Do you also wish to go away?” It is one of the loneliest questions in the Gospel, and Jesus does not soften what he has said in order to keep them. Simon Peter answers for them all: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God.” Peter does not claim to understand everything. He has simply looked at every other road and found that none of them leads to life. St John Chrysostom notes that Peter's words are not those of a man with nowhere else to go but of a man who loves: who else, he means, will teach us such things (Homilies on John 47, in substance). St Augustine observed that Peter says “we have come to believe and know” and not the other way round: we believe in order to understand (Tractates on John 27, in substance). That is the faith we bring to the Holy Qurbono every Sunday. We do not see how bread becomes his Body; we believe his word, and the believing opens our eyes.

St Paul gives thanks for the same kind of faith in the Thessalonians: “We also constantly give thanks to God for this, that when you received the word of God that you heard from us, you accepted it not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word, which is also at work in you believers.” The word of God is not only read; it works. It changes those who receive it. The Catechism takes up this very verse to say that the Church welcomes Sacred Scripture not as a human word but as the word of God, and finds in it her nourishment and her strength (CCC 104). The verses that follow speak with pain of opponents in Judea who had resisted the apostles. Paul, himself a son of Israel who loved his people deeply (Romans 9:1-5), is describing particular adversaries of his own day. The Church teaches firmly that what happened in the Passion of Christ cannot be charged against all the Jews then living, nor against the Jews of today, and that the Jewish people must never be presented as rejected or accursed by God (Nostra Aetate 4; CCC 597). We read such passages with that teaching, and with humility, because every one of us has also resisted the word at times.

Today the Panchangam remembers a saint in whom that word worked with joy: St Philip Neri. Born in Florence in 1515, he came to Rome as a young man and lived for years as a layman, teaching, visiting the sick in the hospitals, and praying at night in the catacombs. The tradition of his life records that on the eve of Pentecost 1544, while he prayed in the catacomb of San Sebastiano, he felt the fire of the Holy Spirit enter his heart, and from then on his heart burned with a love that people could almost feel. He founded a confraternity to care for poor pilgrims, was ordained a priest in 1551, and began to gather people in a simple room for prayer, the reading of Scripture, the lives of the saints and music. From those meetings came the Congregation of the Oratory, approved by Pope Gregory XIII in 1575. He heard confessions for hours each day, laughed easily, played jokes on himself to keep from pride, and was loved by cardinals and street boys alike. People called him the Apostle of Rome. He died in the early hours of 26 May 1595, after celebrating Corpus Christi, and was canonised in 1622. This week, in the season of Pentecost, he reminds us that the Holy Spirit does not make Christians gloomy. Where the Word is welcomed and the Eucharist is loved, joy follows.
outline: Opening
Ask: when following Jesus becomes hard, where else would I go?
Point 1 · “Do you also wish to go away?”
Many left after the bread of life discourse; the Twelve stayed.
Point 2 · Not a human word but God's word
The word that works in those who receive it.
Point 3 · St Philip Neri: the joy of the Spirit
A heart set on fire at Pentecost, a priest who made Rome smile.
Take-home line
“Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
live: Stay when it is hard (John 6:67–68)
Think of one teaching of the Church you find hard, and instead of walking away, read what the Catechism says about it this week.
Let the word work (1 Thessalonians 2:13)
Read one Gospel passage slowly each evening this week, and ask: what is this word doing in me?
2027-05-26.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Holy One of God, you have the words of eternal life, and you give us your flesh as the bread of life. When others turn away, and when we ourselves are tempted to leave, keep us with you. Let us receive your word not as a human word but as the word of God, at work in us. Through the prayers of St Philip Neri, whose heart you set on fire with your Spirit, fill us with joy in your service, make us humble and cheerful, and draw many to you through our love for the Holy Qurbono. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: Peter's confession is renewed at every Holy Qurbono: we come to the altar because there is nowhere else to go, and the Lord who has the words of eternal life gives us his Body and Blood.
conn: The end of the bread of life discourse.
John 6:25–33, read on the First Sunday after Pentecost, began the teaching on the true bread from heaven; today, in John 6:67–69, the Twelve choose to stay when many leave.
A word at work.
1 Thessalonians 2:13: the word of God works in those who receive it; St Philip Neri's Oratory was built on the daily reading of Scripture and the lives of the saints.
Pentecost fire.
Acts 2:3 tells of tongues as of fire; the life of St Philip Neri records that the fire of the Spirit came into his heart on the eve of Pentecost 1544.
fathers: St John Chrysostom
Peter's answer is not that of a man with nowhere else to go but of one who loves greatly: who else will teach us such things? (Homilies on John 47, in substance).
St Augustine
Peter said we have believed and have known, not we have known and believed: we believe in order to understand (Tractates on John 27, in substance).
magis: Catechism 104
In Sacred Scripture the Church constantly finds her nourishment and her strength, for she welcomes it not as a human word but as what it really is, the word of God.
Dei Verbum 21

The Church has always venerated the divine Scriptures as she venerates the Body of the Lord, never ceasing to offer the faithful the bread of life from the one table of the word of God and of the Body of Christ.
Nostra Aetate 4

What happened in the Passion of Christ cannot be charged against all the Jews then living without distinction, nor against the Jews of today; they are not to be presented as rejected or accursed by God.

2027-05-27.title: Thursday of the first week after Pentecost
readings: Seek the things that are above; your life is hidden with Christ in God
The woman who touched the fringe of his clothes: “Daughter, your faith has made you well”
2027-05-27.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the First Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-05-27.verse: for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.
theo: Three weeks ago we kept Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord, and saw him go up in glory. St Paul draws from that mystery a rule for daily life: “So if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God. Set your minds on things that are above, not on things that are on earth.” Paul is not telling us to despise the earth, to neglect our work or our families. He is telling us where to set the compass. A person whose heart is fixed on Christ at the Father's right hand works, studies, cooks and cares for the sick in a different way, because none of it is the last word. St Augustine, preaching on the Ascension, said that Christ is now exalted above the heavens and yet still feels on earth the sufferings of his members, and that we, while we are still here, may already be with him there by faith, hope and love (Sermon on the Ascension of the Lord, in substance). Then comes the line that describes every baptized person: “for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God. When Christ who is your life is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory.” In Baptism we went down into the water with Christ and rose with him. The deepest part of our life is now hidden, kept safe with Christ in God, like a seed under the soil. It will be seen on the day he appears.

The Gospel shows what it looks like when someone seeks Christ with her whole heart. Jesus returns across the lake, and the crowd welcomes him, “for they were all waiting for him.” A leader of the synagogue named Jairus falls at his feet and begs him to come to his house, “for he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, who was dying.” On the way, the crowds press in on him. And in that crush is a woman whom nobody notices. She “had been suffering from hemorrhages for twelve years; and though she had spent all she had on physicians, no one could cure her.” For twelve years, as long as Jairus' daughter had been alive, she had been weak, poor and, by the law of purity, kept at a distance from others. “She came up behind him and touched the fringe of his clothes, and immediately her hemorrhage stopped.” The fringe was the tassel that every faithful Jewish man wore on the corners of his cloak, as the Law commanded (Numbers 15:38): Jesus, a son of Israel, wore it too, and through it the power of God reached her. Then Jesus asks, “Who touched me?” Peter is almost amused: “Master, the crowds surround you and press in on you.” But Jesus says: “Someone touched me; for I noticed that power had gone out from me.” St Augustine put the difference in a few words: the crowd presses, faith touches (Sermons, in substance). Many were close to Jesus that day; one touched him.

Jesus does not let her slip away healed but hidden. “When the woman saw that she could not remain hidden, she came trembling; and falling down before him, she declared in the presence of all the people why she had touched him, and how she had been immediately healed.” Jesus wants more than her body to be healed. He wants her to be restored to the community, and above all he wants to meet her. “He said to her, ‘Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace.’” Daughter: no one had called her that for twelve years. That word is the second healing. Today our Syro-Malabar brothers and sisters keep the feast of the Body and Blood of Christ, and in many countries the Latin Church keeps Corpus Christi on this Thursday too; in India the Latin Church keeps it on Sunday. Whatever the calendar, the Gospel tells us what happens at every Holy Qurbono. We come in a crowd, and it is possible to stand very near the altar and only press. Or we can come as she came, from behind, with nothing but need and faith, and touch him. When we receive his Body and Blood, power goes out from him into us. And he wants to say to each of us what he said to her: your faith has made you well; go in peace.
outline: Opening
Ask: at the Holy Qurbono, am I only pressing in the crowd, or do I reach out and touch Christ?
Point 1 · Seek the things that are above
The compass of a life raised with Christ.
Point 2 · Your life is hidden with Christ in God
Baptism hides our true life in God, to be revealed in glory.
Point 3 · The crowd presses, faith touches
The woman who reached out, and the Lord who called her daughter.
Take-home line
“Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace.”
live: Set the compass (Colossians 3:2)
Before you begin your work today, say: Lord, let me do this for you, who are seated at the right hand of the Father.
Touch him with faith (Luke 8:44)
At your next Holy Qurbono, bring one hidden need with you and, as you receive, place it in his hands.
2027-05-27.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, risen and ascended, you are seated at the right hand of the Father, and our life is hidden with you in God. Turn our hearts to the things that are above, so that we may do our earthly work with heavenly hope. As the woman reached out to touch the fringe of your clothes, let us come to you with humble faith, especially in the Holy Qurbono. Let your power go out to heal the sick, the ashamed and the forgotten, and speak to each of us your word of peace. When you appear in glory, may we appear with you. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the hidden life is given: under the forms of bread and wine the ascended Christ comes to his members, and those who receive him in faith touch more than the fringe of his clothes.

2027-05-28.title: Friday of the first week after Pentecost
readings: Timothy sent to strengthen and encourage you, so that no one would be shaken
The poor widow put in everything she had, all she had to live on
2027-05-28.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the First Sunday after Pentecost.
2027-05-28.verse: she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on.
theo: St Paul had founded the church in Thessalonica in a hurry. Within weeks trouble broke out, and he had to leave the city by night, leaving behind a handful of new believers who had only just been baptized. He worried about them constantly. In today's Epistle he tells them what he did: “Therefore when we could bear it no longer, we decided to be left alone in Athens; and we sent Timothy, our brother and co-worker for God in proclaiming the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you for the sake of your faith, so that no one would be shaken by these persecutions.” Paul gives up the company he needed so that they might have the help they needed. He sends his best helper. This is what a pastor's heart looks like, and it is what the Church still does: a bishop sends a priest to a distant parish, a parish sends catechists to the children, a family sends a son or daughter to serve the Church in a far place. Paul is honest about the cost of the Christian life: “Indeed, you yourselves know that this is what we are destined for. In fact, when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we were to suffer persecution; so it turned out, as you know.” He never sold the gospel as an easy road. On this Friday, the day our Church keeps in memory of the Cross, we remember that every disciple walks behind a crucified Lord.

Paul's fear is not that they will suffer, but that they will give up: “For this reason, when I could bear it no longer, I sent to find out about your faith; I was afraid that somehow the tempter had tempted you and that our labor had been in vain.” The tempter rarely needs to make us deny Christ in one dramatic moment. More often he works by tiredness and discouragement: the long illness, the unemployment, the mocking at work, the slow cooling of prayer. Against this the Church does what Paul did. She sends people to strengthen one another. Every one of us can be a Timothy to someone: a phone call to a family going through trouble, a visit to a young person who has stopped coming to the Qurbono, an hour with a neighbour who has lost heart. Hebrews says: “let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds.” Encouragement is not a small thing. It can keep a faith alive.

The Gospel moves from Paul's anxious love to a quiet scene in the temple. Jesus “sat down opposite the treasury, and watched the crowd putting money into the treasury. Many rich people put in large sums. A poor widow came and put in two small copper coins, which are worth a penny.” No one else notices her. But Jesus calls his disciples and says: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all those who are contributing to the treasury. For all of them have contributed out of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on.” God does not measure the gift by its size but by what it costs and by the trust it shows. The widow gave her whole living, and in doing so she placed herself in God's hands. St Cyprian of Carthage, urging his people to give to the poor, held up this widow to the wealthy as a reproach and an example: if she, poor and alone, gave all she had, what excuse have those who have plenty (On Works and Almsgiving 15, in substance)? The Catechism sees in her the poverty of heart that Jesus asks of his disciples (CCC 2544). And on this Friday we see in her a picture of the Lord himself, who a few days later in the same city gave not two coins but his whole life on the Cross. When we bring our offering to the altar, whether it is large or small, let it be a sign that we give ourselves.
outline: Opening
Ask: do I give God what is left over, or what costs me something?
Point 1 · Sent to strengthen and encourage
Paul gives up his helper so that the young church may stand firm.
Point 2 · So that no one would be shaken
The tempter works by discouragement; the Church answers by encouragement.
Point 3 · Everything she had
The widow's two coins, and the Lord who gave his whole life.
Take-home line
“She out of her poverty has put in everything she had.”
live: Be a Timothy (1 Thessalonians 3:2)
Call or visit one person this week who is going through a hard time, and encourage them in faith.
Give what costs (Mark 12:44)
Give something this week, money, time or effort, that you will actually feel, for the poor or for the Church.
2027-05-28.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, on the Cross you gave your whole life for us, holding nothing back. Teach us to give as the poor widow gave, not from what we do not need but from what we have, trusting in the Father's care. Make us like Timothy, sent to strengthen and encourage those who are shaken by trials. Guard all who suffer for your name from the tempter's discouragement, and let our offering at the altar be the offering of our whole selves. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the gift of the widow is perfected: the Lord who gave everything on the Cross makes his one sacrifice present in the Holy Qurbono, and our small gifts are joined to his.

2027-05-29.title: Saturday of the first week after Pentecost · St Theodosia
readings: Appoint elders in every town: a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple
2027-05-29.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the First Sunday after Pentecost. The Panchangam remembers St Theodosia; it does not say which saint of that name is meant. Tomorrow, the Second Sunday after Pentecost, is Vocations Day.
2027-05-29.verse: Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.
theo: Tomorrow our Church keeps Vocations Day, and today's Epistle could hardly be more fitting. St Paul has left his co-worker Titus on the island of Crete with a task: “I left you behind in Crete for this reason, so that you should put in order what remained to be done, and should appoint elders in every town, as I directed you.” The young churches of Crete needed shepherds, and Paul did not leave the choice to chance. He lists what such a man must be: “For a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless; he must not be arrogant or quick-tempered or addicted to wine or violent or greedy for gain; but he must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled.” Then the most important quality: “He must have a firm grasp of the word that is trustworthy in accordance with the teaching, so that he may be able both to preach with sound doctrine and to refute those who contradict it.” From the beginning the Church has been built on the apostles and on those they appointed to succeed them. St Ignatius of Antioch, writing on the way to his martyrdom, told the Christians of Smyrna: where the bishop appears, there let the people be, just as where Jesus Christ is, there is the Catholic Church (Letter to the Smyrnaeans 8, in substance). Our own Church has lived this through every generation, from the first bishops to those who shepherd us today.

Paul's list is demanding, and it is meant to be. A bishop is called “God's steward”: the household is not his, it belongs to God, and he will give an account. But the list is also a mirror for every Christian. Hospitality, goodness, prudence, self-control, a firm hold on the faith: these are not only for bishops and priests. And they are learned first at home. Where do priests and religious come from? From families where the evening prayer is kept, where the Qurbono is the centre of Sunday, where a child sees a father who is not quick-tempered and a mother who loves goodness, where the priest is welcomed and prayed for. If our parishes lack vocations, the first question is not about seminaries but about our homes. Tomorrow, on Vocations Day, pray by name for the young people of your parish, and ask whether God may be calling someone in your own family. And pray for the priests and bishops we already have, that they may be the stewards Paul describes.

The Gospel tells us the price of every vocation, lay or ordained. “Now large crowds were traveling with him; and he turned and said to them, ‘Whoever comes to me and does not hate father and mother, wife and children, brothers and sisters, yes, and even life itself, cannot be my disciple. Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.’” The word “hate” is a Semitic way of speaking about what comes first; St Matthew gives the same saying as loving father or mother “more than me” (Matthew 10:37). Jesus does not ask us to stop loving our families; he asks that no love, not even love of our own life, be placed above him. The Imitation of Christ calls this the royal road of the holy Cross, and says that in the Cross is life and protection from our enemies (Book II, 12, in substance). The Panchangam today remembers St Theodosia. It does not tell us which of the holy women of that name is meant. One whose story is well attested is Theodosia of Tyre: Eusebius of Caesarea records that during the persecution of 307 a young Christian girl from Tyre, not yet eighteen, went up to the confessors who were on trial at Caesarea, greeted them and asked them to remember her when they came before the Lord; for this she was arrested, cruelly tortured and drowned in the sea (The Martyrs of Palestine 7, in substance). Whether or not she is the saint our Church names today, her courage shows what the Gospel means: she loved Christ more than her own life, and she carried the cross to the end.
outline: Opening
Ask: what comes first in my life, before even my family and my own life?
Point 1 · Elders in every town
Paul sends Titus to give the young churches shepherds.
Point 2 · God's steward
The bishop's virtues are a mirror for every home where vocations are born.
Point 3 · Carry the cross and follow
The price of discipleship, and the courage of a young martyr named Theodosia.
Take-home line
“Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
live: Pray for shepherds (Titus 1:5)
Tomorrow, on Vocations Day, pray by name for two young people of your parish and for your parish priest.
Put Christ first (Luke 14:26)
Name one thing you love that has begun to come before Christ, and give it its right place this week.
2027-05-29.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, Good Shepherd, you sent your apostles to appoint shepherds in every town. Give your Church bishops and priests after your own heart: blameless stewards, hospitable and self-controlled, holding firm to your trustworthy word. Bless our families, so that from them may come men and women ready to serve you. Give us the grace to love you above all things and to carry our cross each day behind you. Through the prayers of St Theodosia and all who loved you more than their own lives, keep us faithful to the end. You live and reign for ever. Amen.
altar: The shepherds whom the apostles appointed stand at the altar in every generation: through the bishop and the priests the one sacrifice of Christ is offered, and the flock is fed with the Body of the Lord who carried his cross for us.

2027-05-31.title: Monday of the second week after Pentecost
readings: Your faith is growing abundantly, and your love for one another is increasing
“This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent”
2027-05-31.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Second Sunday after Pentecost. No commemoration is printed in the Panchangam. The Latin Church keeps today the feast of the Visitation of the Blessed Virgin Mary, and the month of May, dedicated to the Mother of God, comes to an end.
2027-05-31.verse: And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.
theo: The Gospel today takes us into the upper room on the night before the Passion. Jesus has finished his long farewell to the disciples, and now he turns to the Father: “After Jesus had spoken these words, he looked up to heaven and said, ‘Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.’” The hour is the hour of the Cross. Jesus calls it the hour of glory, because on the Cross the love of the Father and the Son will be shown to the whole world. Then he tells us what all his work has been for: “And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” Eternal life is not only life that goes on for ever after death. It begins now, and its heart is knowing God: not knowing about him, as we know facts from a book, but knowing him as a child knows its father and a friend knows a friend. St Irenaeus put it in words the Church has never forgotten: the glory of God is a human being fully alive, and the life of a human being is the vision of God (Against Heresies IV, 20, 7, in substance). Every Holy Qurbono, every prayer of the Shehimo, every page of the Gospel read in faith is a step deeper into that knowing.

Jesus ends: “I glorified you on earth by finishing the work that you gave me to do. So now, Father, glorify me in your own presence with the glory that I had in your presence before the world existed.” The Son who speaks is not a creature who has earned a reward. He shared the Father's glory before the world began; he is God from God, light from light. Now, having taken our flesh and finished his work, he asks that this flesh, our human nature, be taken into that glory. This is what we celebrated at Suloko and at Pentecost: the risen Lord in glory at the Father's side, and the Spirit sent so that we may share his life. St Paul's prayer for the Thessalonians shows what that life looks like when it takes root in a community: “We must always give thanks to God for you, brothers and sisters, as is right, because your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing.” Knowing God and loving one another grow together. A parish where faith is growing will be a parish where the love of its members is growing too.

Paul adds that this growth is taking place under pressure: “Therefore we ourselves boast of you among the churches of God for your steadfastness and faith during all your persecutions and the afflictions that you are enduring.” He speaks of God's justice, that God will one day give “relief to the afflicted as well as to us, when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with his mighty angels.” Christians do not take revenge; they leave judgement to God and pray for those who wrong them, as Jesus did on the Cross. Today is the last day of May, the month our people dedicate to the Mother of God, and the Latin Church keeps the feast of the Visitation. No one knew Jesus more deeply than his holy Mother. She carried him in her womb to the hill country, and Elizabeth greeted her: “blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.” As the month of Mary closes, ask her to teach you what the Gospel calls eternal life: to know the Father and the Son whom he sent, to believe his word as she did, and to carry Christ to others in haste and in love.
outline: Opening
Ask: do I know about God, or do I know God?
Point 1 · Faith growing, love increasing
Paul's thanksgiving for a church that grows under pressure.
Point 2 · This is eternal life
To know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent.
Point 3 · The hour of glory, and the Mother who believed
The Son glorified with the glory he had before the world; Mary who knew him best.
Take-home line
“This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God.”
live: Know him, not only about him (John 17:3)
Spend ten minutes today speaking to God in your own words, as to a Father, before any set prayer.
Let love increase (2 Thessalonians 1:3)
Do one act of kindness today for someone in your parish or family whom you do not usually notice.
2027-05-31.prayer: Father, the only true God, you sent your Son Jesus Christ, and in him you have given us eternal life: to know you and the one whom you have sent. As he glorified you on earth by finishing your work, let us glorify you by our faith and our love. Make our faith grow abundantly and our love for one another increase, even in affliction. With the holy Mother of God, who believed your word and carried your Son in haste to others, let us know your Son more deeply and bring him to those we meet. Through Jesus Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: At the altar the hour of glory is made present: the Son who glorified the Father by finishing his work offers his one sacrifice, and in the Holy Qurbono we begin to know God with the knowledge that is eternal life.

quick: “Your pain will turn into joy”: Easter joy is born through the Cross.
No one can take away the joy that rests on the risen Christ.
The Spirit of truth will guide us into all truth.
2027-05-02.action: Each evening this week thank God for three joys of the day.
2027-05-02.question: What steals my joy, and how can Christ give it back?
2027-05-02.special: Fifth Sunday after Qyomtho. Announce Suloko (Ascension) on Thursday 6 May.
illus: An illustration
In a Kerala hospital a young mother, exhausted after a long labour, holds her newborn and smiles: “I've forgotten all the pain.” Jesus used exactly this picture for the joy of Easter.

family.explain: Jesus told his friends they would be sad when he died, but their sadness would turn into joy when they saw him again. And nobody can take that joy away!
family.intention: We pray for people who are sad, that they may find joy in Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What made each of us happy this week? Let's thank God.”

kidsaint: St Athanasius (2 May)
A bishop of Alexandria who bravely taught that Jesus is truly God, even when he was sent away from his city five times. Lesson: stay true to Jesus even when it is hard.
term: The fifty days
From Qyomtho to Pentecost the Church keeps fifty days of Easter joy, like Israel's fifty days from Passover to the feast of weeks (Deuteronomy 16:9–12).
termMore: Jesus' name for the Holy Spirit in John (14:17; 16:13): the Spirit who leads the Church into the fullness of truth.

quick: Jesus ascends with hands raised in blessing.
Our humanity has entered heaven: where the Head is, the body hopes to follow.
Not gazing upwards, but going out: the Ascension leads to mission.
2027-05-06.action: Pray every day until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit.”
2027-05-06.question: Is my heart lifted up to the Lord, or only looking at earthly things?
2027-05-06.special: Suloko, the Ascension of our Lord: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. Ten days of prayer until Pentecost (no marriage celebrations, as in the lectionary).
illus: An illustration

When a Kerala father leaves for work abroad, the family gathers at the door and he raises his hand to bless the children before the car leaves. They remember that blessing for months. Jesus left his disciples with his hands raised in blessing, and he has never lowered them.

family.explain: Forty days after Easter, Jesus blessed his friends and went up to heaven. He is with God the Father, and he still blesses us. He promised to send the Holy Spirit.
family.intention: We pray for families separated by work abroad, and for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we pray together for the Holy Spirit these ten days?”

kidsaint: The prophet Elisha

When his teacher Elijah was taken up to heaven, Elisha picked up his cloak and received his spirit to carry on God's work. Lesson: when Jesus went to heaven, he gave us his Spirit to continue his work.
term: Suloko (സുലൂക്കോ)
Syriac for “ascension”: the feast of the Ascension of our Lord, forty days after Qyomtho, always on a Thursday.
termMore: Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church prays, like the apostles with Mary in the upper room (Acts 1:14), for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

quick: “It is to your advantage that I go away”: the Spirit will make Christ present everywhere.
The Church waits in prayer with Mary.
“Be strong and courageous; the Lord is with you.”
2027-05-09.action: Pray each day until Pentecost for one gift of the Holy Spirit.
2027-05-09.question: Which gift of the Holy Spirit do I most need?
2027-05-09.special: Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho. Announce Pentecost next Sunday. (In 2025–26 also Social Communication Media Day; check the collection.)
illus: An illustration

Before a big family wedding in Kerala, relatives gather in the house days earlier to pray the Rosary each evening. The house becomes an upper room. That is what the Church does between the Ascension and Pentecost.

family.explain: After Jesus went to heaven, his friends prayed together with Mary, waiting for the Holy Spirit Jesus had promised.
family.intention: We pray for the gifts of the Holy Spirit for each of us.
family.ask: Ask: “Which gift of the Spirit do we need most in our family?”

catechism: The gifts of the Holy Spirit.
kidsaint: Mary in the upper room
After Jesus went to heaven, Mary prayed with the apostles, waiting for the Holy Spirit. She is the Mother of the Church. Lesson: pray with Mary, and the Spirit will come.
term: Social Communication Day
In the 2025–26 lectionary the Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho was Social Communication Media Day, when the Church prays for the right use of the media.
termMore: John 17, the prayer of Jesus to the Father at the Last Supper, is called his “high-priestly prayer”: for his glory, for his disciples, and for all who will believe.

quick: Pentecost: the Spirit comes as wind and fire; the Church is born into mission.
Babel reversed: one Spirit, many languages, all nations.
A new heart and a new spirit: the Spirit is poured on all the baptised.
2027-05-16.action: Offer one of your gifts to the service of your parish this month.
2027-05-16.question: Am I living by the power of the Holy Spirit, or as if he had never come?
2027-05-16.special: The Sunday of Pentecost: day of obligation; Holy Qurbono for the people. The season of Pentecost begins.
illus: An illustration

At a Kerala charismatic retreat centre, people from every state of India pray together in Malayalam, Tamil, Hindi, Konkani and English, and yet it feels like one prayer. That is Pentecost: one Spirit, many tongues.

family.explain: On Pentecost the Holy Spirit came on the apostles like a strong wind and tongues of fire. They became brave and told everyone about Jesus in many languages!
family.intention: We pray for the Holy Spirit to fill our family with love and courage.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift has God given each of us to help others?”

catechism: Chrismation and the gift of the Spirit.
kidsaint: St Philip Neri (26 May)
A joyful priest of Rome who loved the Holy Spirit and made young people laugh while teaching them to pray. People called him the apostle of Rome. Lesson: the Holy Spirit gives joy.
term: Pentecost

Greek for “fiftieth”: the fiftieth day after Qyomtho, when the Holy Spirit came upon the apostles and Mary (Acts 2). In the West Syriac tradition the Pentecost service includes solemn prayers on bended knee for the gift of the Spirit.
termMore: The fifth season of the Syro-Malankara year, from Pentecost until the Transfiguration season: the time of the Church's mission in the power of the Spirit.

quick: After Pentecost: the Spirit bears fruit in us.
Be good soil: hear the Word, hold it fast, bear fruit with patience.
Work for the bread that endures: believe in the One God has sent.
2027-05-23.action: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately this week.
2027-05-23.question: What kind of soil is my heart for God's Word?
2027-05-23.special: First Sunday after Pentecost. (In 2025–26 also Vocation Day; check the collection.)
illus: An illustration

Kerala farmers know that seed sown on laterite rock dries up, while the same seed in the paddy field brings a harvest. The difference is the soil, not the seed. The Spirit sows the same Word in all of us.

family.explain: The Holy Spirit helps good things grow in us, like fruit on a tree: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control.
family.intention: We pray that the fruit of the Spirit may grow in our family.
family.ask: Ask: “Which fruit of the Spirit will each of us practise this week?”

kidsaint: St Mariam Thresia

A Syro-Malabar sister from Thrissur who visited poor families, cared for the sick and the dying, and founded the Congregation of the Holy Family. The fruit of the Spirit was seen in her kindness. Lesson: let your kindness show God's love.
term: The season of Pentecost
The season after Pentecost when the Church, filled with the Spirit, grows and bears fruit. In the Syro-Malankara year it leads into the season of the Transfiguration.
termMore: The Friday after Pentecost, when the lectionary reads the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk” (Acts 3:6).

quick: The Spirit is poured out on all who call on the Lord.
“No condemnation for those in Christ Jesus”: the Spirit gives life.
“Be holy”: the cross carried with love and the cup of water given in his name.
2027-05-30.action: Do one small, hidden act of kindness each day this week in Jesus' name.
2027-05-30.question: Which beatitude is God asking me to live now?
illus: An illustration
In many Kerala homes a pot of water is kept by the gate in summer for anyone passing by. No one sees who fills it. Jesus says not even that cup of water will lose its reward.

family.explain: Jesus says even giving a cup of water to someone in his name is precious to God. Small kindnesses matter!
family.intention: We pray to be holy and kind, as God is holy.
family.ask: Ask: “What small kindness can each of us do this week?”

kidsaint: The Twelve Apostles

Jesus prayed all night and then chose twelve ordinary men: fishermen, a tax collector and others. With the Holy Spirit they carried the Gospel to the whole world, and St Thomas came to India. Lesson: God chooses ordinary people for great things.
term: Beatitudes
The blessings with which Jesus begins his teaching (Matthew 5; Luke 6). Luke gives four blessings and four woes. They describe the happiness of those who belong to God's kingdom.
termMore: After Pentecost the lectionary reads how the Spirit forms the Church: the apostles' preaching in Acts, Paul's teaching on life in the Spirit, and Jesus' calling and sending of disciples.

quick: Mar Yauseph, Patron of Workers, is remembered on May Day; Jesus was known in his town as the carpenter's son.
Paul worked night and day to burden no one and taught: anyone unwilling to work should not eat.
Jeremiah the Prophet, rejected by his own town, learned at the potter's wheel that Israel is clay in God's hand.
2027-05-01.action: Do one piece of today's work with extra care and offer it to God.
2027-05-01.question: Do I see my daily work as something I offer to God, or only as something I must get through?
term: Nbiya (നബിയാ)
The Syriac word for prophet. Our Panchangam names Jeremiah as Yeremiah Nbiya, one who speaks God's word to his people.
kidsaint: St Joseph the worker

St Joseph was a carpenter in Nazareth. He made doors, tables and ploughs, and he taught the boy Jesus to use a saw and a hammer. He worked hard and honestly so that Jesus and Mary had what they needed. Lesson: when you do your homework or help at home carefully, you are working like St Joseph, and Jesus is pleased.

family.explain: When Jesus came back to his home town, people said: “Isn't he the carpenter's son?” St Joseph was a carpenter, and Jesus grew up helping him in the workshop. God's own Son did ordinary work with his hands! Today is Labour Day, and our Church remembers St Joseph the worker. Every honest job, at home, in the field, in an office or a kitchen, can be done for God.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who works for our family, and for people who have no work.
family.ask: Ask: “What work did each of us do this week? How can we do it for Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A headload worker at a timber depot near Punalur carried logs for thirty-one years. His son, now an engineer in Kochi, remembers how his father came home every evening with sore shoulders and still washed his hands and feet before joining the family prayer. Once, when the boy complained that his father's job was not respectable, the father showed him the small picture of St Joseph he kept in his shirt pocket. “He was a working man too,” he said, “and God trusted him with Jesus.” On the day the son received his first salary, he bought his father a new picture frame for that same worn picture.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, carpenter of Nazareth, bless our work and make it a prayer to the Father. Amen.
share: Is not this the carpenter’s son? (Matthew 13:55). What does it mean to me that Jesus spent most of his life working?
We worked night and day, so that we might not burden any of you (2 Thessalonians 3:8). Whom does my work support, and do I burden anyone unfairly?
Within me there is something like a burning fire (Jeremiah 20:9). What word of God burns in me and asks to be spoken?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Yauseph, bless the work of our hands, O Lord.
interc: For all workers on this Labour Day, especially daily-wage labourers, farmers and migrant workers, that they may receive a just wage and be treated with dignity.
For those without work, that they may find honest employment, and for employers, that they may be just.
For workers who are in danger at sea, in factories, on building sites and on the roads.
For prophets and preachers who are not welcomed, that they may stay faithful like Jeremiah.
For our parish, that our work and our worship may be one offering to God.
pm.close: Father, your Son was known as the carpenter's son and was obedient to Mar Yauseph in Nazareth. Through the prayers of St Joseph and of Jeremiah your prophet, make our work holy, our hearts open to your word, and our lives an offering pleasing to you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: do not receive the grace of God in vain; now is the acceptable time, now is the day of salvation.
The apostle's life is full of paradox: sorrowful yet always rejoicing, poor yet making many rich, having nothing yet possessing everything.
Jesus says in the temple: I am the light of the world; whoever follows me will have the light of life.
2027-05-03.action: Do today one good thing for God that you have been putting off.
2027-05-03.question: What am I postponing until a better time, when God is asking for it now?

family.explain: Jesus said, “I am the light of the world.” When the power goes off at night, we quickly look for a torch or a lamp, because in the dark we can trip and fall. Sin is like darkness: it makes us lose our way. Jesus is our light: when we follow him, we can see where to walk. St Paul also tells us not to wait: today is the day to be good and to love God.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel lost or sad, that Jesus may be their light.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there something good we keep saying we will do later? Can we do it this week?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in Mavelikara kept a list on her fridge titled “When I have time.” It held visiting her estranged sister, joining the parish prayer group, and learning the evening prayer of the Shehimo by heart. Each year the list grew. During a long stay in hospital she read 2 Corinthians 6:2, and on the morning she came home she crossed out the title and wrote “Now.” Her sister came for lunch that Sunday. They had not spoken for nine years.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, light of the world, shine in our hearts and teach us to answer your grace today. Amen.
share: Do not accept the grace of God in vain (2 Corinthians 6:1). What grace have I received that I am letting go to waste?
As sorrowful, yet always rejoicing (2 Corinthians 6:10). When have I known joy in the middle of sorrow?
Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness (John 8:12). Where do I need Christ's light most today?
pm.resp: Lord, our light and our salvation, hear us.
interc: For those who keep postponing their return to God, that they may hear that today is the day of salvation.
For missionaries and priests who live in hardship, that they may possess everything in Christ.
For the poor who make others rich by their faith and patience.
For those who live in darkness of addiction, despair or sin, that the light of Christ may reach them.
For our parish, as we prepare for Suloko and pray for the coming of the Holy Spirit.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son as the light of the world and testified to him. Let us not receive your grace in vain, but walk in his light today, rejoicing even in sorrow, until we see his glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul preached at Thessalonica with courage in God, seeking to please not mortals but God who tests our hearts.
He was gentle like a nurse and firm like a father, sharing not only the Gospel but his own self.
Jesus answers insult with truth: whoever keeps my word will never see death.
2027-05-04.action: Give someone an unhurried hour of your time this week.
2027-05-04.question: Do I share only words about God, or also my time and my life?

family.explain: St Paul says he was gentle with the people of Thessalonica, like a nurse taking care of little children. He loved them so much that he gave them not only the good news of Jesus but his own time and his whole heart. In a family we do this for one another every day: mothers, fathers, grandparents and children all care for each other.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, teachers and parents, that they may be gentle and strong like St Paul.
family.ask: Ask: “Who in our family needs more of our time this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young priest was sent to a small parish in the hills of Idukki where many families had moved away. In his first months he preached careful sermons and few people came. An old sacristan advised him: “Father, before they listen to you, they need to see you.” So he began walking every afternoon to two or three houses, sitting on the veranda, drinking the black tea he was given and listening to stories of rubber prices and children abroad. By the next Easter the church was fuller. One woman told him, “We came because you came first.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, your word is life. Teach us to keep it and to share it with our whole lives. Amen.
share: We speak, not to please mortals, but to please God who tests our hearts (1 Thessalonians 2:4). Whom am I trying to please?
Gentle among you, like a nurse tenderly caring for her own children (1 Thessalonians 2:7). Who has cared for my faith with such tenderness?
Whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). Which word of Jesus am I trying to keep this week?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us in your word.
interc: For bishops, priests and catechists, that they may share the Gospel and their own selves with their people.
For parents and grandparents, who pass on the faith with gentleness and firmness.
For those who are insulted or misunderstood for doing good, that they may answer like Jesus, with truth and without bitterness.
For friendship and respect between Christians and the Jewish people.
For the dying, that they may hold to the word of Christ and pass through death into life.
pm.close: Father, your Son honoured you in all things and promised life to those who keep his word. Give us pure hearts that seek only your pleasure, and generous hearts that share themselves with others, until we see you face to face. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul asks the Thessalonians to pray that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified everywhere.
The Lord is faithful; he will strengthen us and guard us from the evil one, and direct our hearts to the love of God and the steadfastness of Christ.
Jesus: your eye is the lamp of your body; if your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light.
2027-05-05.action: Pray today by name for your bishop, your parish priest and one missionary.
2027-05-05.question: What do my eyes take in each day, and does it fill me with light or with darkness?

family.explain: When we light the nilavilakku in the evening, we put it in the middle of the room, not under the bed, so everyone can see. Jesus says our eyes are like a lamp: if we look at good things, our whole body is full of light. If we look at bad things, we fill ourselves with darkness. Tomorrow we celebrate Jesus going up to heaven, and he wants us to be his light in the world.
family.intention: We pray for our priests and missionaries who carry Jesus' word to people far away.
family.ask: Ask: “What good things did our eyes see today? Is there anything we should stop watching?”

illus: An illustration

A family in Kottarakkara noticed that their evening prayer had become shorter and shorter, squeezed between television serials and phones. One evening the youngest child asked why the nilavilakku was now lit in the corner behind the sofa, where no one could see it. The father moved it back to the centre of the room. Without any rule being made, the family began to switch off the screens when the lamp was lit, and the prayer slowly grew long again. The grandmother said it was the lamp that taught them.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you are faithful. Guard us from the evil one and fill our eyes and hearts with your light. Amen.
share: Pray for us, so that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly (2 Thessalonians 3:1). For whom will I pray, that the word may spread through them?
May the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the steadfastness of Christ (2 Thessalonians 3:5). Where does my heart need straightening?
Consider whether the light in you is not darkness (Luke 11:35). What darkens my eyes and my heart?
pm.resp: Faithful Lord, strengthen us and guard us.
interc: For our bishops, priests and missionaries, that the word of the Lord may spread through them and be glorified.
For persecuted Christians, that the faithful Lord may strengthen and guard them from evil.
For all who struggle with temptations of the eyes, impurity or addiction to screens, that they may receive a healthy eye.
For families, that the evening lamp and the evening prayer may keep their place at the centre of the home.
For our parish as we celebrate Suloko tomorrow, that we may lift our hearts to the Lord.
pm.close: Father, you are faithful in all your promises. As we prepare to celebrate the Ascension of your Son, let his word run through the world, guard us from the evil one, and make us lamps that shine with his light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Panchangam keeps today the Finding of the Cross; by about 350 St Cyril of Jerusalem spoke of fragments of the wood spread through the world, and tradition links the finding with St Helena.
Paul boasts of nothing but the Cross, by which the world is crucified to him; what matters is a new creation.
The kingdom is a treasure hidden in a field; on this First Friday we honour the pierced Heart of Jesus.
2027-05-07.action: Make the sign of the Cross slowly and attentively each time you pray today.
2027-05-07.question: What do I really boast of, and does it lead me to the Cross or away from it?
term: Sleeba (സ്ലീബാ)
The Syriac word for the Cross. In our Church the bare Sleeba, without a figure, stands on the altar and is used for blessing, proclaiming that the Crucified One is risen.
kidsaint: St Helena and the Cross

St Helena was the mother of the emperor Constantine. When she was old, she travelled to Jerusalem to visit the places where Jesus had lived, died and risen. An old story tells that she searched on the hill of Calvary and found the Cross of Jesus. Lesson: every time you make the sign of the Cross, you are holding up the greatest treasure in the world, the sign of Jesus' love.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a man who found a treasure hidden in a field. He was so happy that he sold everything he had to buy that field! Today our Church remembers the finding of the Cross of Jesus. The Cross is our treasure, because on it Jesus showed how much he loves us. It is also First Friday, when we remember the Heart of Jesus, full of love for us.
family.intention: We pray for people who are carrying a heavy cross of sickness, sadness or poverty.
family.ask: Ask: “What is our family's greatest treasure? How can we show that Jesus is the most important?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Thiruvalla wore a small wooden cross on a thread for forty years, long after her friends had moved to gold chains. When her grandson asked why she did not wear something more beautiful, she told him that her mother had given it to her the day she left home to work as a nurse in the Gulf. On nights in a strange land, when she was afraid or lonely, she held it in her hand. “Gold I could lose,” she said. “This kept me.” The day she died, the family placed the same little cross in her hands.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world. Let us boast of nothing but your Cross. Amen.
share: May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ (Galatians 6:14). What do I boast of instead?
In his joy he goes and sells all that he has (Matthew 13:44). What would I give up for the treasure of Christ?
I carry the marks of Jesus branded on my body (Galatians 6:17). What marks of suffering for Christ do I carry, and how can I offer them?
pm.resp: We adore you, O Christ, and we bless you, because by your holy Cross you have redeemed the world.
interc: For all who carry heavy crosses of illness, loss or poverty, that they may find in the Cross of Christ their strength.
For Christians in the Holy Land and in Jerusalem, where the Cross was raised and found.
For those who are ashamed of their faith, that they may sign themselves openly with the Cross.
On this First Friday, for sinners, that the pierced Heart of Jesus may draw them to repentance.
For our parish in these days of waiting, that we may receive the Holy Spirit with open hearts.
pm.close: Father, you willed that your Son should save the world by the Cross. As we honour the finding of the holy Cross, grant that we may share in its mystery here on earth and enjoy its fruit, the risen life, in heaven. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Mar Yohannan Shleeha, son of Zebedee, is known in the Church's tradition as the beloved disciple and the evangelist of the fourth Gospel.
Paul: nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
The Congregation of the Daughters of Mary was founded on 8 May 1938 at Marthandam; like John, its sisters took the Mother of the Lord into their home.
2027-05-08.action: Do one hidden act of love today for someone hard to love.
2027-05-08.question: Am I comparing my road with someone else's, instead of simply following Jesus?
term: Shleeha (ശ്ലീഹാ)
The Syriac word for apostle, one who is sent. Our Church names the apostles with this title: Mar Yohannan Shleeha, Mar Yaqob Shleeha, Mar Thoma Shleeha.
kidsaint: St John, the beloved disciple

St John was a young fisherman whom Jesus called to follow him. At the Last Supper he leaned close to Jesus, and on Good Friday he stayed at the Cross when others ran away. Jesus gave him Mother Mary to take care of. When John was very old, he kept telling everyone: “Little children, love one another.” Lesson: stay close to Jesus, love Mother Mary, and love one another.

family.explain: Today we remember St John, the friend whom Jesus loved. He stayed with Jesus at the Cross, and Jesus gave him his own Mother: “Here is your mother.” John took Mother Mary into his home. St Paul says nothing can ever separate us from Jesus' love, not sadness, not danger, not even death. Today we also thank God for the Sisters called Daughters of Mary, who work for poor people and for Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for the Sisters in our parish and our Church, and for young people whom God is calling to serve him.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make Mother Mary feel at home in our family?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Marthandam, an old man who had lost his wife and whose sons lived in the city was found one monsoon evening alone in a house with a leaking roof and no food. Two sisters of a religious congregation who visited the sick in that area came by on their rounds. They did not preach. They mended what they could, cooked rice and stayed until he slept. They kept coming every week for two years. When the parish priest later asked him what had brought him back to the Qurbono after decades, he said, “They kept coming. I understood that someone loved me who did not need me.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you loved Mar Yohannan and gave him your Mother. Keep us in your love, from which nothing can separate us. Amen.
share: Peter turned and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them (John 21:20). What helps me to follow Jesus closely, as John did?
Who will separate us from the love of Christ? (Romans 8:35). What fears make me doubt his love?
Here is your mother (John 19:27). How does Mary have a place in my home and my prayer?
pm.resp: By the prayers of Mar Yohannan Shleeha, keep us in your love, O Lord.
interc: For our Church, that like Mar Yohannan we may be witnesses whose testimony is true.
For the Congregation of the Daughters of Mary and all religious sisters, in thanksgiving for their service, and for new vocations.
For families, that they may take Mary, the Mother of God, into their homes.
For those who feel separated from God's love by suffering, persecution or sin.
For the elderly and lonely, that someone may come to them with the love of Christ.
pm.close: Father, through Mar Yohannan Shleeha you opened to us the mystery of your Word made flesh. Grant that we may understand what he taught, love as he loved, and with Mary the Mother of your Son wait in prayer for the gift of the Holy Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Simon the Zealot, one of the Twelve, waited in the upper room with Mary for the Spirit; Jesus turned his zeal towards the Kingdom.
Zacchaeus the tax collector climbed a tree to see Jesus; Jesus called him by name and salvation came to his house.
Paul stayed in Ephesus until Pentecost because a wide door had opened; holy zeal is patient, prayerful and gentle.
2027-05-10.action: Pray by name for one person you have given up on, and ask Jesus to stop at that person's house.
2027-05-10.question: Is my zeal for God turned against people, or towards the lost?
term: Shleeha (ശ്ലീഹാ)

The Syriac word for apostle, meaning one who is sent. Our Church gives this title to the Twelve, to St Paul, and to those whom tradition counts among the first preachers, such as Mar Shemun Shleeha and Mar Addai Shleeha.
kidsaint: St Simon, the apostle with a fiery heart

Simon was called “the Zealot,” which means he was full of zeal, a burning love for God. Before he met Jesus, he may have wanted to fight the Romans. Jesus taught him a better way: to love even people he did not like, like Matthew, who had been a tax collector. Simon learned to put his fire into telling everyone about Jesus. Lesson: when you feel strongly about something, ask Jesus to turn that strong feeling into love.

family.explain: Zacchaeus was a short man who climbed a tree to see Jesus. Everyone thought he was a bad man, but Jesus called him by name and went to his house. Zacchaeus was so happy that he gave half of what he had to the poor and paid back everyone he had cheated.
family.intention: We pray for someone who seems far from God, that Jesus may visit that person's home.
family.ask: Ask: “If Jesus said today, ‘I must stay at your house,’ what would we want to put right first?”

illus: An illustration

In a town near Adoor there was a man the neighbours called “the moneylender.” His interest was high and his heart seemed hard. A young parish priest, new to the town, began to stop at his gate every evening on the way back from the house blessings, only to greet him and ask after his health. For months the man answered with a grunt. Then one evening, during the days before Pentecost, he invited the priest in. “Everyone else crosses the road when they see me,” he said. “Why do you stop?” The priest answered, “Because Jesus stopped under a tree in Jericho.” Within a year the old man had cancelled the debts of two widows and was coming to the Holy Qurbono on Sundays. No sermon had changed him. A man who kept stopping at his gate had.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you came to seek the lost. As we wait for your Holy Spirit, stop at our house today and call each of us by name. Amen.
share: Simon, who was called the Zealot (Luke 6:15). What am I zealous about, and how could Jesus turn that zeal towards his Kingdom?
Zacchaeus, hurry and come down; for I must stay at your house today (Luke 19:5). Where in my life is Jesus asking me to come down quickly?
A wide door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many adversaries (1 Corinthians 16:9). What door is God opening for our prayer group?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church in these days before Pentecost, that like the apostles we may wait in prayer with Mary for the Holy Spirit.
For those who have strayed from the faith and those whom others have given up on, that the Lord may find them.
For tax officials, business people and all who handle money, that they may be honest and generous to the poor.
For young people who serve in our parish, that no one may despise them and that they may grow in courage.
For the Churches that honour St Simon, that his prayers may keep them zealous for the Gospel.
pm.close: Lord Jesus, you made the Zealot and the tax collector brothers at your table. Make our zeal gentle and our hearts open, and send your Spirit upon us. Amen.

quick: Jesus spent the night in prayer, then chose the Twelve; every mission is born from prayer.
Sts Cyril and Methodius gave the Slav peoples an alphabet, the Gospels and the Liturgy in their own language.
God's plan is to gather all things in Christ, and the Holy Spirit is the seal and pledge of that gathering.
2027-05-11.action: Pray tonight for a people or language group in India that has not yet heard the Gospel in its own tongue.
2027-05-11.question: Do I treasure the prayers of my Church enough to hand them on to the next generation?
kidsaint: Two brothers and a new alphabet

Long ago two brothers, Cyril and Methodius, were asked to teach people in a faraway land about Jesus. But those people had no letters to write their language! So Cyril invented a whole new alphabet. Then the brothers wrote the Gospels and the prayers of the Church in that language, so that everyone could understand. Lesson: God speaks every language, and he wants every person to hear his love in words they understand.

family.explain: Before Jesus chose his twelve apostles, he went up a mountain and prayed to his Father all night long. In the morning he called twelve men by name. Today we also remember two brothers who carried the message of Jesus to a faraway people and wrote it down in their language.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries who learn new languages to tell people about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Which of us will learn a new prayer this week and teach it to the rest of the family?”

illus: An illustration

A young sister from Changanassery was sent to a mission station in the hills of Arunachal Pradesh. For the first months she understood almost nothing the villagers said, and they smiled politely at her Malayalam and her halting Hindi. So she sat each evening with an old woman of the village, pointing at things and writing down the words in a notebook. After two years she could tell the story of the Good Shepherd in the village language. The first time she did, the old woman wept and said, “I did not know God could speak like us.” The notebook is still kept in the convent. On its first page the sister had written a single line: “Lord, give me their words, so that I may give them yours.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Holy Spirit, promised by the Father, come and seal us as your own. Teach us to pray in the language of our hearts. Amen.
share: He spent the night in prayer to God (Luke 6:12). How do I prepare in prayer for the important choices of my life?
To gather up all things in him, things in heaven and things on earth (Ephesians 1:10). Whom is God asking me to bring into his family?
Marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit (Ephesians 1:13). How can I live this week as one who bears God's seal?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church in these days before Pentecost, that the Holy Spirit may make her one in every language and culture.
For missionaries, translators of Scripture and teachers of catechism, that their words may carry the Word.
For the peoples of Eastern Europe, that by the prayers of Sts Cyril and Methodius they may grow in faith and in peace.
For our children and young people, that they may love the prayers and hymns of our Church.
For unity among Christians of East and West, that we may praise God with one heart.
pm.close: Father, in Christ you gather all things to yourself. Seal us with your Spirit and make us one family of every tongue, to the praise of your glory. Amen.

quick: Mar Yaqob of Nisibis, a Father of Nicaea, and Mar Epiphanios of Cyprus guarded the true faith; Epiphanios taught: honour Mary, worship God alone.
Paul: work out your salvation, for God is at work in you; shine like stars without murmuring.
Jesus: read the present time, and make peace with your accuser while you are still on the way.
2027-05-12.action: Make one step towards peace with someone before Pentecost.
2027-05-12.question: Am I reading the signs of God in this present time, or only the weather?
kidsaint: The bishop and his medicine chest

St Epiphanius was a bishop on the island of Cyprus long ago. He wrote a big book called “the medicine chest.” It was not for coughs and fevers! It was for wrong ideas about God. For each wrong idea he wrote down the true teaching of the apostles, like a medicine. He taught that we love and honour Mother Mary very much, but we worship only God. Lesson: when someone says something about Jesus that sounds wrong, ask your parents or your catechism teacher for the true answer.

family.explain: Jesus said that people can look at the clouds and know that rain is coming. But they did not notice that God was doing something wonderful right in front of them. Right now the Church is waiting for the Holy Spirit to come at Pentecost.
family.intention: We pray that our family may notice the ways God is working in our home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone our family needs to make peace with before Pentecost?”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in a village near Kottarakkara had not spoken for six years over a strip of land between their houses. Each May, when the first monsoon clouds gathered over the hills, their old mother would say, “The rain is coming; are you ready?” She meant the roofs and the drains. One year, in the week before Pentecost, the younger brother heard her say it and suddenly understood it differently. He walked across the disputed strip, knocked on his brother's door, and said, “Let us settle it before the rain.” They divided the land with a row of banana plants. On Pentecost Sunday the old mother sat between her two sons at the Holy Qurbono. “This year,” she told the neighbours, “the rain came into my house.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord God, you are at work in us. Open our eyes to read this present time, and make us ready for your Holy Spirit. Amen.
share: It is God who is at work in you (Philippians 2:13). Where have I seen God at work in me this week?
Do all things without murmuring and arguing (Philippians 2:14). What do I complain about most, and how can I offer it to God instead?
On the way make an effort to settle the case (Luke 12:58). With whom do I need to make peace now?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church in these days before Pentecost, that she may read the signs of the times and be ready for the Spirit.
For bishops and teachers of the faith, that like Mar Yaqob and Mar Epiphanios they may guard the true faith with love.
For all who are in disputes over land, money or family matters, that they may settle them in peace.
For farmers waiting for the monsoon, that the rains may come in good measure.
For our parish, that we may shine like stars in the world by our joy and our honesty.
pm.close: Father, you who began a good work in us will bring it to completion. Make us blameless children of light, and pour out your Spirit upon us. Amen.

quick: On the great day of the feast Jesus cried out: let the thirsty come to me; he spoke of the Spirit, given once he was glorified.
Hebrews: God swore by himself; our hope is an anchor fixed behind the curtain, where Jesus our forerunner has entered.
Mar Ishaq Malpan of Antioch, a fifth-century Syriac teacher and poet, taught the Church to pray in song.
2027-05-13.action: Learn by heart Hebrews 6:19, “We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
2027-05-13.question: Where have I thrown the anchor of my hope: into passing things, or into Christ?
term: Malpan (മല്പാൻ)

The Syriac word for teacher. Our Church gives this title to great teachers of the faith, such as Mar Yaqob of Nisibis and Mar Ishaq of Antioch, and it is still used for priests who teach in seminaries.

family.explain: Jesus said that anyone who is thirsty can come to him and drink. He was not talking about ordinary water. He was talking about the Holy Spirit, who would come like a river into the hearts of those who believe. At Pentecost, this coming Sunday, we celebrate that gift.
family.intention: We pray for everyone who is thirsty for God, that they may come to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When we drink water today, can we say a little prayer: ‘Jesus, give us your Spirit’?”

illus: An illustration

A fisherman from Neendakara once explained to his grandson why he trusted his old anchor more than his new engine. “The engine can stop,” he said, “the net can tear, the sky can turn black. But when the anchor bites the bottom, the boat swings round and faces the waves, and it does not drift onto the rocks.” Years later the grandson, now a young priest, preached on Hebrews 6 at a Holy Qurbono for fishermen's families. He held up a small anchor his grandfather had left him. “Our anchor,” he said, “does not go down into the mud. It goes up, behind the curtain, into the hands of Jesus. When the storm comes, we do not drift. We turn and face it.”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you call the thirsty to yourself. We come thirsting for your Holy Spirit. Fill us, and make our hope firm in you. Amen.
share: Let anyone who is thirsty come to me (John 7:37). What is my heart thirsting for at this moment?
We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul (Hebrews 6:19). What storm in my life needs this anchor?
Abraham, having patiently endured, obtained the promise (Hebrews 6:15). Which promise of God am I still waiting for in patience?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church as she waits for Pentecost, that she may thirst for the Holy Spirit and receive him in abundance.
For those who have lost hope, through illness, debt or grief, that Christ may be their anchor.
For fishermen and all who work at sea, that God may protect them in storms.
For teachers of prayer, poets and church musicians, that like Mar Ishaq Malpan they may help the faithful to pray.
For the dry places of our world and of our hearts, that the living water of the Spirit may flow there.
pm.close: Father, you swore by yourself and your promise cannot fail. Anchor our hope in Christ, who has gone before us, and pour your Spirit into our thirsty hearts. Amen.

quick: Mar Addai, sent after the Ascension by Thomas to Edessa, founded the Church there; Syriac Christianity, and our own tradition, flows from that apostolic spring.
Jesus: what is whispered will be proclaimed from the housetops; do not fear, for even the sparrows are not forgotten.
Paul: I have learned contentment; I can do all things through him who strengthens me; you did well to share my distress.
2027-05-14.action: Support or contact one missionary from your parish or eparchy before Pentecost.
2027-05-14.question: What fear keeps me from speaking of Jesus where I live and work?
term: Addai (അദ്ദായി)

The Syriac form of the name Thaddaeus. Syriac tradition counts Mar Addai among the Seventy (or Seventy-two) disciples sent by the Lord, and honours him as the apostle of Edessa, with his disciples Aggai and Mari.
kidsaint: Mar Addai and the sick king

Long ago a king named Abgar lived in the city of Edessa. He was very sick, and he had heard that Jesus could heal people. The old story says that after Jesus went up to heaven, the apostle Thomas sent a disciple named Addai to the king. Addai prayed for the king, the king was healed, and many people in Edessa came to believe in Jesus. Lesson: Jesus still sends his friends to bring his love to people who are sick or sad. You can be one of them!

family.explain: Jesus says that God knows even the little sparrows, which people bought for just a few coins. And he knows us even better: he has counted every hair on our heads! So we do not need to be afraid. Today we remember Mar Addai, who was not afraid to go to a faraway city to tell people about Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries and for all who are afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes each of us afraid, and how can remembering God's love help us?”

illus: An illustration

A retired teacher in Kollam kept a small bird feeder outside her kitchen window. Each morning sparrows came and argued over the rice. When her grandson was preparing for a difficult entrance examination and could not sleep for fear, she brought him to the window. “Count them,” she said.
