He counted seven. “Your God knows each one of these,” she told him, “and none of them is worried about tomorrow. And Jesus says you are worth more than many sparrows.” He laughed, but he slept that night. Years later, working as a doctor in a mission hospital in Bihar, he kept a photograph of that bird feeder on his desk. Under it he had written Luke 12:7.

pm.open: Christ is risen! Lord Jesus, you sent your apostles after your Ascension. Take away our fear and send your Holy Spirit upon us, so that we may be your witnesses. Amen.
share: What you have whispered behind closed doors will be proclaimed from the housetops (Luke 12:3). What would I want proclaimed about my faith?
Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows (Luke 12:7). Which fear do I need to hand over to God tonight?
I can do all things through him who strengthens me (Philippians 4:13). Where do I need Christ's strength this week?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church on the threshold of Pentecost, that like Mar Addai she may go out without fear to all peoples.
For the Churches of the Syriac tradition in the Middle East, especially in the lands of ancient Edessa, that they may live and worship in peace and safety.
For missionaries from Kerala serving in other states and countries, that we may share their distress by our prayers and gifts.
For all who live in fear, of illness, of violence, of the future, that they may know they are counted in God's hands.
For the sick, that like King Abgar they may receive healing and faith.
pm.close: Father, not one sparrow is forgotten before you. Strengthen us in Christ, make us content and generous, and send us out as witnesses of your Son. Amen.

quick: Today the Panchangam remembers the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain: Mary is the field that bore the Bread of life.
Jesus: blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it; Mary did so first and best.
Paul: sow bountifully; God loves a cheerful giver. St Pachomius became a monk after strangers brought him bread in prison.
2027-05-15.action: Give something today, gladly, to someone who is hungry.
2027-05-15.question: Do I keep God's word in my heart as Mary did, or do I only hear it?
term: Yoldath Aloho (ദൈവമാതാവ്)

Syriac for “she who gave birth to God,” the Mother of God (Greek Theotokos). The Church confessed this title at the Council of Ephesus in 431, because the child Mary bore is the eternal Son of God made man.
kidsaint: St Pachomius and the bread in the night

Pachomius was a young soldier who was locked in a prison with other young men. One night some strangers came with bread and water for them. Pachomius asked, “Who are these kind people?” Someone told him, “They are Christians.” He was so touched that he decided to become a Christian and spend his life helping others. Later he started big homes where many monks lived, prayed and worked together. Lesson: a small kindness, like sharing food, can change someone's whole life.

family.explain: A woman in the crowd shouted that Jesus' mother was very blessed. Jesus said that people who hear God's word and do what it says are blessed too. Mother Mary did that better than anyone. Today our Church also thanks God for the grain growing in the fields, which becomes our bread.
family.intention: We pray for farmers, for the coming harvest, and for all who do not have enough to eat.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share with someone who is hungry this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a paddy village near Kuttanad, an old farmer had a custom his grandchildren found strange. When the first ears of rice appeared each season, he would cut a few stalks, tie them with a thread and take them to the parish church, where he laid them quietly before the icon of the Mother of God. “She gave us the Bread,” he would say, “so I bring her the first bread.” One year the harvest failed in the neighbouring fields because of floods, and his own was small. Still he took the first stalks to church, and afterwards he sent half his rice to the families who had lost everything. His grandson asked why he gave so much when they had so little. The old man laughed: “The one who sows bountifully reaps bountifully. Have you ever seen the Mother of God let a cheerful giver go hungry?”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Holy Mother of God, you heard the word of God and kept it, and you waited with the apostles for the Spirit. Pray for us tonight, on the eve of Pentecost. Amen.
share: Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it (Luke 11:28). Which word of God am I being asked to keep this week?
The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). Where am I sowing sparingly?
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food (2 Corinthians 9:10). For which gifts of the harvest do I need to thank God?
pm.resp: Risen Lord, hear our prayer.
interc: For the Church on the eve of Pentecost, that with Mary she may receive the Holy Spirit in fullness.
For farmers and farm workers, for the coming monsoon and the harvest, that the earth may yield its increase.
For the hungry and for all who share their bread, that God may multiply their seed.
For Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios on his name day, and for all our bishops, that they may be faithful shepherds.
For monks and sisters, that like St Pachomius they may live in prayer, work and sharing.
pm.close: Father, through the Mother of God you gave us the Bread of life. Make us hear and keep your word, give cheerfully, and wait with her for your Holy Spirit. Amen.

quick: The season of Pentecost begins: the Church that has received the Spirit is sent out.
Paul asks the Philippians to live as worthy citizens of the gospel, side by side and unafraid.
Jesus sends the Twelve with nothing in their belts: what they received as gift they must give as gift.
2027-05-17.action: Do one hidden service today for which you expect nothing in return.
2027-05-17.question: What have I received without payment that I am still keeping to myself?

family.explain: Jesus sent his twelve friends to tell people that God's kingdom was near and to heal the sick. He told them not to take money or extra clothes. Everything they had, God had given them for nothing, so they should give it to others for nothing too. Yesterday was Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit came; now the Spirit sends us out to share.
family.intention: We pray for the sick in our family and our parish, and for all who carry the good news to others.
family.ask: Ask: “What has God given each of us that we can share with someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A retired mathematics teacher in a village near Kottarakkara noticed that several children in his parish were failing in school because their parents could not pay for tuition. After the evening prayer one Pentecost Sunday he told the vicar he would teach any child who came, every evening, on the verandah of the parish hall, and he would take nothing. Some parents tried to pay him with bananas and jackfruit; he gave them to the children. When people asked why, he said only: someone taught me for nothing when I was a poor boy, and the Lord said, you received without payment, give without payment. Eight years later two of those children were teaching on the same verandah.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have poured out your Spirit and you send us out. Make us worthy of your gospel and generous with your gifts. Amen.
share: Live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27). Where does my life not yet match the gospel?
Striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel (Philippians 1:27). With whom do I need to stand side by side?
You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). What can I give this week?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out in the power of your Spirit.
interc: For the Church, that in this season of Pentecost she may go out with courage to proclaim the kingdom.
For missionaries, catechists and all who serve without payment.
For Christians who face opponents because of their faith, that they may not be intimidated.
For the sick, that the healing love of Jesus may reach them through his disciples.
For our parish, that we may work side by side with one mind.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to proclaim your kingdom and your Spirit to make us his witnesses. Make our lives worthy of the gospel, keep us united and unafraid, and let us give as generously as we have received. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Hebrews: the Son shared our flesh and blood, to destroy death's power and become a merciful and faithful high priest.
Because he himself was tested, he can help us when we are tested.
Jesus compares God to a woman who lights a lamp and sweeps the house until she finds one lost coin.
2027-05-18.action: Reach out today to one person you had written off as lost.
2027-05-18.question: Do I believe that Jesus understands my temptations from the inside?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a woman who had ten silver coins and lost one. She did not say, I still have nine. She lit a lamp, swept the whole house and looked everywhere until she found it, and then she had a party with her friends. Jesus says God is like that: when one person comes back to him, heaven has a party too.
family.intention: We pray for anyone we know who has gone away from God or from our family, that they may come home.
family.ask: Ask: “Who might be feeling lost or left out, and how can we help them feel found?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in a parish near Mavelikara lost the small gold cross her mother had given her on her wedding day. She searched the house for two days; her husband said it was only a small thing and he would buy her another. On the third evening she took a torch, moved every piece of furniture in the bedroom and swept the floor inch by inch. She found it in a crack beside the door frame. That Sunday she told the vicar about it, a little embarrassed. He smiled and said: now you know how God searches for each of us. It was never about the price of the gold. It was about whose gift it was.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you shared our flesh and blood and you search for every one of us. Make us your lamp to seek the lost. Amen.
share: He himself likewise shared the same things (Hebrews 2:14). Where do I most need to know that Jesus shares my life?
He is able to help those who are being tested (Hebrews 2:18). What test do I bring to him tonight?
Rejoice with me, for I have found the coin that I had lost (Luke 15:9). Whose return do I long to celebrate?
pm.resp: Merciful High Priest, help us.
interc: For all who are being tested by temptation, illness or grief, that they may know the help of Jesus.
For those who have drifted from the Church, that the Spirit may search them out and bring them home.
For priests, that they may share the mercy of the High Priest in the sacrament of Confession.
For the poor, for whom one coin can mean a day's food.
For our parish, that we may never be content with nine coins and forget the tenth.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to share our flesh and blood and to seek what was lost. Keep us close to him in every trial, and make us eager to search for those who have strayed, so that heaven may rejoice over them. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Our Church remembers today the first offering of the Holy Qurbono by Mar Yaqob Shleeha; tradition honours St James of Jerusalem, to whom the Anaphora of St James is ascribed.
St Paul hands on what he received: the Lord's words over the bread and the cup, “Do this in remembrance of me.”
In Luke the Lord says, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you”: the Qurbono is his longing to give himself to us.
2027-05-19.action: Come early to your next Holy Qurbono and prepare in silence.
2027-05-19.question: Do I come to the Qurbono as one whom the Lord eagerly desired to feed?
term: Qurbono (കുർബാന)
The Syriac word for offering or sacrifice, from a root meaning to draw near. The Holy Qurbono is the Eucharistic sacrifice, in which we draw near to God through the offering of Christ.
kidsaint: St James, the man with camel knees

St James was a relative of Jesus and became the first bishop of Jerusalem. An old writer says he prayed on his knees so much that his knees became hard like a camel's! Our Church remembers that he offered the Holy Qurbono, and the prayer of our Qurbono is called by his name. Lesson: when you kneel and pray, you are doing what St James did.

family.explain: At the Last Supper Jesus took bread and said, This is my body, which is given for you. Then he took the cup and said, This cup is the new covenant in my blood. He told his friends to do this to remember him. Today our Church remembers St James, who offered the Holy Qurbono in Jerusalem long ago. Every time our priest offers the Qurbono, Jesus gives himself to us in the same way.
family.intention: We pray for our priests, and for children preparing for their First Holy Communion.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get ready as a family for the next Qurbono?”

illus: An illustration

A young priest was posted to a small mission station in the hills of Idukki, where only eleven families came to the Qurbono. In his first month he felt that his years of study were wasted on so few. One morning an old man who had walked an hour in the rain stayed behind after the Qurbono and said: Achen, for thirty years we had the Qurbono here only once a month; now we have it every day. I prayed for this before you were born. The priest went back to the altar after the man had left and knelt there for a long time. He said later that it was the day he learned that no Qurbono is small.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you longed to share the Passover with your disciples. Give us a longing for your holy Mysteries. Amen.
share: I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you (1 Corinthians 11:23). Who handed on the faith of the Qurbono to me?
I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you (Luke 22:15). How do I prepare to meet the Lord who longs for me?
You proclaim the Lord's death until he comes (1 Corinthians 11:26). What does my life proclaim after the Qurbono?
pm.resp: Lord, make us worthy of your holy Mysteries.
interc: For all bishops and priests, that they may offer the Holy Qurbono with faith and reverence.
For those who have stopped coming to the Qurbono, that they may hunger for it again.
For children preparing for First Holy Communion and for their families.
For Christians who cannot attend the Qurbono because of persecution, distance or illness.
For our parish, that the Qurbono may be the centre of our life.
pm.close: Father, through Mar Yaqob Shleeha and the apostles you handed on to your Church the holy Mysteries of the Body and Blood of your Son. Keep us faithful to them, make us long for them, and through them prepare us for the wedding feast of the Lamb. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Today our Church honours the Four Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John: four Gospels, one Christ.
St Paul: faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
The risen Lord sends the eleven to make disciples of all nations and promises, “I am with you always.”
2027-05-20.action: Begin reading one Gospel today, one chapter a day.
2027-05-20.question: How much of the Gospel have I actually heard, read and taken to heart?
term: Evangelion (ഏവൻഗേലിയോൻ)
The Greek word for Gospel, meaning good news. In our Church the Gospel reading of the Holy Qurbono is called the Evangelion; it is proclaimed by the priest while the people stand.
kidsaint: The four evangelists and their animals

Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote the four Gospels about Jesus. In church pictures each has a sign: Matthew a man, because he begins with Jesus' family; Mark a lion, because he begins with John the Baptist's loud voice in the desert; Luke an ox, because he begins in the temple where animals were offered; John an eagle, because he flies high to tell us that Jesus is God. Lesson: four writers, one Jesus. Which Gospel will you read?

family.explain: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John wrote down the life and words of Jesus so that we could know him. At the end of Matthew's Gospel, Jesus sends his friends to teach everyone about him and promises, I am with you always. Whenever we read the Gospel, Jesus is speaking to us.
family.intention: We pray for all who translate, teach and preach the Gospel, and for people who have never heard of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Shall we read a little of a Gospel together every evening this week? Which one shall we start with?”

illus: An illustration

A grandfather in Thiruvalla had a habit that his grandchildren found strange: every evening after the prayer he read one chapter of a Gospel aloud, even if only the cat was listening. When he died, the family found his Bible worn soft at the edges. Inside the cover, in his small handwriting, was a list of dates: every time he had finished reading all four Gospels, from the year of his marriage. There were forty-one dates. His eldest grandson, then working abroad, took the Bible with him. A year later he wrote home that he had begun his own list.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, through the four evangelists you speak to us. Open our ears to hear you and our lips to proclaim you. Amen.
share: How are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? (Romans 10:14). Who first proclaimed Jesus to me?
How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news! (Romans 10:15). To whom can I bring good news this week?
I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matthew 28:20). When have I felt the Lord with me through his word?
pm.resp: Lord, let your word go out to all the earth.
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim the Gospel to all nations with courage and joy.
For Bible translators, teachers of Scripture and catechists.
For those who have never heard the name of Jesus, that someone may be sent to them.
For the Jewish people, the first to hear the word of God, that they may grow in faithfulness to his covenant.
For our families, that the Gospel may be read and loved in our homes.
pm.close: Father, through the evangelists you gave your Church the Gospel of your Son. Let their words take root in our hearts, make us messengers with beautiful feet, and keep us in the company of the risen Lord who is with us always. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Golden Friday, the first Friday after Pentecost, remembers the first miracle of the apostles in the name of Jesus: the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate.
Peter: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk.”
Paul: without love, even miracles and generosity are nothing; Jesus: for God all things are possible.
St Helena, mother of Constantine, spent the wealth of an empire on churches in the Holy Land and on the poor.
2027-05-21.action: Give one person today what you have: your time, your help, a hand to lift them up.
2027-05-21.question: What is my gold, and is it in the hands of Jesus?
term: Golden Friday (സ്വർണ്ണ വെള്ളിയാഴ്ച)

The first Friday after Pentecost in our Syriac tradition, on which the Church remembers the first miracle of the apostles after Pentecost, the healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate (Acts 3). The name is commonly linked to St Peter's words, “I have no silver or gold.”
kidsaint: St Helena, the queen who built churches

Helena was the mother of Constantine, the first Roman emperor to become a Christian. When she was an old lady she travelled all the way to the land where Jesus lived. She built churches in Bethlehem, where Jesus was born, and on the Mount of Olives, where he went up to heaven, and she gave money to many poor people. Lesson: whatever you have, a little or a lot, you can use it for Jesus.

family.explain: After the Holy Spirit came, Peter and John went to the temple to pray. A man who had never walked was sitting at the gate, asking for money. Peter said, I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you: in the name of Jesus, stand up and walk! The man jumped up and went into the temple, walking and leaping and praising God. Today is Golden Friday, the day we remember this first miracle after Pentecost.
family.intention: We pray for people who cannot walk, for the sick, and for the poor who sit at the gates of our churches.
family.ask: Ask: “We may not have much money, but what do we have that we can give someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A beggar sat every Sunday at the gate of a church in Pathanamthitta district, and for years the parishioners dropped coins into his bowl on their way in. One Golden Friday a group of young people from the parish youth movement stopped instead of passing by. They asked his name, which no one had done before. They learned that he had been a mason until an accident ruined his leg. Over the following months they found him a doctor, then a lighter job at a building site run by a parishioner. A year later he came in through the same gate, walking with a stick, and sat in the church for the first time. He told the vicar: for years people gave me coins; these children gave me back my place.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, in your name the lame man stood up and walked. On this Golden Friday fill us with your love, and make us give what we have in your name. Amen.
share: I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you (Acts 3:6). What do I have that I can give?
If I... do not have love, I am nothing (1 Corinthians 13:2). Where is my service empty of love?
For God all things are possible (Matthew 19:26). What seems impossible to me that I should entrust to God?
pm.resp: In the name of Jesus, raise us up.
interc: For the Church, that her true gold may always be the name of Jesus and the love of the poor.
For people with disabilities and the chronically ill, that they may find healing, dignity and a place in our communities.
For the rich, that their hearts may be made generous, and for the poor, that they may receive what they need.
For our parish youth, that they may stop, look and lift up those at the gate.
For all who bear the name Helena, and for all mothers who lead their children to Christ.
pm.close: Father, on this Golden Friday you show us that the name of your Son is worth more than silver and gold. Fill us with the love without which we are nothing, loosen our hold on what we own, and make us generous like St Helena and bold like your apostles. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: the Christians of Corinth are a letter of Christ, written by the Spirit of the living God on human hearts.
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life: the Spirit gives the strength to do what God commands.
The wise bridesmaids kept oil for their lamps; St Rita's patient faith burned through a long night of suffering.
2027-05-22.action: Do one hidden work of mercy today to keep your lamp filled.
2027-05-22.question: What does my life say about Christ to those who read it?
kidsaint: St Rita and the rose in winter

Rita lived in Italy long ago. Her husband was often angry, but she was gentle and prayed for him, and he became kinder. Later she became a nun. An old story says that when she was dying in winter she asked for a rose from her garden, and her cousin found one blooming in the snow. That is why people give roses on her feast. Lesson: patience and prayer can make beautiful things grow even in hard times.

family.explain: Jesus told a story about ten girls waiting with lamps for a wedding. Five brought extra oil and five did not. The bridegroom came late at night, and the lamps of the five without oil were going out, so they missed the party. Jesus wants us to be ready for him always, with our lamps full: full of prayer and kindness every day, not only at the last minute.
family.intention: We pray for families who are going through hard times, and for anyone who feels their problem is impossible.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one way each of us can put oil in our lamp this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a town in central Kerala a woman lived for many years with a husband who drank and shouted. Her neighbours told her to leave; her own brothers were ready to deal with him. Every Saturday she lit a candle before a small picture of St Rita and prayed the same prayer: give me patience, and give him a new heart. Her children grew up hearing her forgive. When her husband fell seriously ill, it was she who sat by him in the hospital. One night he asked a priest to hear his confession. Afterwards he said to her: all those years you were the only Bible I read. She did not tell anyone that for a long time; she said only that the candle had been worth it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, by your Spirit you write on our hearts. Make our lives letters of your love, and keep our lamps burning. Amen.
share: You yourselves are our letter... to be known and read by all (2 Corinthians 3:2). What do people read in me?
The letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Where do I need the Spirit's strength to do what I know is right?
Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13). Is my lamp ready?
pm.resp: Come, Holy Spirit, write on our hearts.
interc: For the Church, that her members may be letters of Christ read by all.
For couples whose marriage is under strain, that by the prayers of St Rita they may find patience, healing and peace.
For those who have been wronged, that they may have the grace to forgive and to refuse revenge.
For all who face impossible causes, that they may not lose hope.
For our parish as we begin the First Sunday after Pentecost, that our lamps may be full.
pm.close: Father, through your Spirit you write your law on our hearts and keep our lamps burning in the night. Make us faithful letters of your Son, give us the patience and forgiveness of St Rita, and keep us ready for the coming of the Bridegroom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Ephesians: through Christ we are no longer strangers but citizens with the saints and members of the household of God.
The Holy Spirit joins us together into a holy temple, a dwelling place for God.
Some believed in Jesus but would not confess it, because they loved human glory more than the glory that comes from God.
2027-05-24.action: Do one small, visible thing today that shows you belong to Christ.
2027-05-24.question: Where do I keep my faith hidden because I am afraid of what others will think?

family.explain: St Paul says the Church is like a house that God is building, and each of us is a stone in it. Jesus is the most important stone, the cornerstone that holds the walls together. The Holy Spirit is the builder who fits the stones next to each other. A stone that will not sit beside the others makes a gap in the wall, so we must learn to live kindly with one another.
family.intention: We pray for our parish family, that we may be one house where God loves to live.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a stone next to me that I find hard to fit with, and what can I do for that person this week?”

illus: An illustration

When a new church was being built in a parish near Kottarakkara, the builders laid the granite blocks of the foundation without mortar for a day, just to see how they would sit. The blocks were heavy and uneven, and one of the old masons spent the whole afternoon chipping a little here and a little there until each block lay flat against its neighbour. A boy watching him asked why he did not simply fill the gaps with cement. The mason said: cement holds for some years, but stones that are shaped to fit each other hold for a hundred. Then he tapped the corner block and added: and everything begins from this one. The parish priest told the story at the dedication, and said that the Holy Spirit works in the same patient way with us.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, builder of the house of God. Fit us together in love, and make us bold to confess Jesus before others. Amen.
share: You are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God (Ephesians 2:19). When did I first feel at home in the Church?
In him the whole structure is joined together (Ephesians 2:21). With whom do I find it hard to be joined together?
They loved human glory more than the glory that comes from God (John 12:43). Whose approval do I seek most?
pm.resp: Lord, build us into your house.
interc: For the Church throughout the world, that the Holy Spirit may bind all her members together in charity.
For Christians who are afraid to confess their faith at work or at school, that they may receive courage.
For those who feel like strangers in the parish, newcomers, migrants and the lonely, that they may find a home.
For our bishops and priests, the builders who serve the house of God, that they may build with patience.
For our parish, that we may become a dwelling place where God is glad to live.
pm.close: Father, through your Son you have made us members of your household, and through your Spirit you are building us into a holy temple. Fit us together in love, keep us faithful in confessing your name, and let us seek only the glory that comes from you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul: our outer nature is wasting away, but our inner nature is being renewed day by day.
Our slight, momentary affliction prepares an eternal weight of glory; what cannot be seen is eternal.
The servants were given a pound each and told to trade with it until the master returned.
2027-05-25.action: Use one gift you have neglected for the good of someone else today.
2027-05-25.question: Am I burying the gifts the Lord gave me because I am afraid?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a king who gave his servants some money and said: use this well until I come back. Two servants worked hard and made more. One was afraid and hid it in a cloth. Jesus gives each of us gifts too: our faith, our talents, our time. He wants us to use them for God and for others, not to hide them.
family.intention: We pray that each of us may use our gifts for God and for one another.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one gift God has given you, and how can you use it for someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

A retired schoolteacher in a parish near Mavelikara lost most of her eyesight in her late seventies. She could no longer read the small print of the prayer book, and for some months she sat at home and said she was of no use to anyone. Then the parish priest asked whether she would help the children who were struggling with their Malayalam reading. She could not see the page, but she could hear every mistake. Twice a week, after school, three or four children sat on her veranda and read aloud to her, and she corrected them from memory. Her eyes were failing, she said, but her ears had become young again. When she died, one of those children read the Epistle at her funeral Qurbono without a single mistake.

pm.open: Come, Holy Spirit, renew our inner nature day by day. Give us wisdom to see what cannot be seen and courage to use the gifts you have given us. Amen.
share: Our inner nature is being renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16). Where have I seen God renew someone in weakness or old age?
What can be seen is temporary, but what cannot be seen is eternal (2 Corinthians 4:18). What invisible treasure do I value most?
Do business with these until I come back (Luke 19:13). Which gift of mine is still wrapped in a cloth?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful servants.
interc: For the elderly, the sick and the disabled, that their inner nature may be renewed day by day.
For all who are afraid to use their gifts, that the Spirit may give them courage.
For teachers, catechists and all who pass on the faith, that they may be wise and patient.
For those who suffer long afflictions, that they may see the glory that is coming.
For our parish, that every gift given to us may be used for the kingdom until the Lord returns.
pm.close: Father, you have entrusted your gifts to your servants and you will call us to give an account. Renew us within by your Holy Spirit, teach us the wisdom that sees the eternal, and make us faithful in small things until your Son comes again. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: After the teaching on the bread of life many disciples left; Jesus asked the Twelve, “Do you also wish to go away?”
Peter answered: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
St Paul gives thanks that the Thessalonians received the word as God's word, at work in them; St Philip Neri lived that word with Pentecost joy.
2027-05-26.action: Read today's Gospel once more before you sleep and repeat Peter's words as your prayer.
2027-05-26.question: Is there a teaching of Jesus that tempts me to walk away?

family.explain: Jesus said something hard to understand: that he would give himself as bread for us. Many people did not like it and went away. Jesus asked his twelve friends: are you leaving too? Peter said: where would we go? Only you have the words of eternal life. Today we also remember St Philip Neri, a very happy priest who loved Jesus in the Holy Qurbono and made everyone smile.
family.intention: We pray that our family will always stay close to Jesus, even when it is hard.
family.ask: Ask: “What makes you happy about being a friend of Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Thiruvalla, working in another country, stopped going to church in his second year abroad. Nobody quarrelled with him about it; he simply drifted. One Sunday, out of loneliness, he walked into the only Catholic church near his flat, a big Latin parish where he understood almost nothing of the language. During the Communion he heard the choir sing a hymn in English with Peter's words: Lord, to whom shall we go? He told his mother later on the phone that he had tried every other road for two years, work, friends, money, games, and that none of them had answered anything. He said: I came back because there was nowhere else to go, and then I found that I did not want to go anywhere else.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you have the words of eternal life. Keep us with you, and fill us with the joy of your Holy Spirit, as you filled St Philip Neri. Amen.
share: Do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67). When was I most tempted to leave Jesus?
Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life (John 6:68). What has Jesus given me that nothing else can?
You accepted it not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word (1 Thessalonians 2:13). How has the word of God worked in me?
pm.resp: Lord, keep us with you.
interc: For all who have drifted away from the Church, that they may hear again the words of eternal life.
For the Congregation of the Oratory and all priests who hear confessions, that like St Philip Neri they may bring joy and mercy.
For mutual respect and friendship between Christians and the Jewish people.
For young people far from home, that they may find a parish family wherever they live.
For our parish, that the joy of the Spirit may be seen in us.
pm.close: Father, your Son has the words of eternal life, and you gave St Philip Neri a heart on fire with your Spirit. Let your word work in us, keep us faithful when others turn away, and make us joyful witnesses of your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

term: Oratory (ഓറട്ടറി)

From the Latin word for a place of prayer. St Philip Neri gave this name to his gatherings for prayer, Scripture and music in Rome, and then to the community of priests he founded, the Congregation of the Oratory. The musical form called the oratorio takes its name from the music sung there.
kidsaint: St Philip Neri and the feathers

A story is told that a woman once came to St Philip Neri to confess that she had spread gossip. He told her to pluck a chicken and scatter the feathers along the street, and then to come back. When she returned he said: now go and gather every feather. She said it was impossible, the wind had blown them everywhere. He answered: so it is with the words we say about others. Lesson: say only kind words, because words cannot be taken back.

quick: St Paul: if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is seated at the right hand of God.
Your life is hidden with Christ in God; when he is revealed, you also will be revealed with him in glory.
In the pressing crowd one woman touched Jesus with faith; he called her daughter and sent her away in peace.
2027-05-27.action: Bring one hidden need to the Lord today with the faith of the woman in the Gospel.
2027-05-27.question: Am I only near Jesus, or do I reach out and touch him?

family.explain: A lady had been sick for twelve years and nobody could help her. She thought: if I can just touch his clothes, I will be well. So she came up behind Jesus in a big crowd and touched the edge of his cloak, and she was healed. Jesus stopped and looked for her, because he wanted to meet her. He called her daughter and said: go in peace. Jesus wants to meet each of us like that.
family.intention: We pray for someone we know who has been sick for a long time.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we pray for tonight, so that Jesus may touch them with his healing?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Adoor, an old man in a wheelchair was brought to the Qurbono every Sunday by his grandson. Because of the crowd at the door, they always sat at the very back, near the pillar. One feast day, when the church was full and the aisle was blocked, the grandson said it was no use trying to go forward for Communion. The old man shook his head and whispered the story of the woman who touched the fringe of Jesus' clothes from behind. A few minutes later the priest, who had seen them, came down the side aisle with the Holy Mysteries and gave him Communion where he sat. The old man said afterwards: I went to him from behind, and he turned round and came to me.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are seated at the right hand of the Father, and power goes out from you. We reach out to you in faith. Heal us and give us your peace. Amen.
share: Seek the things that are above, where Christ is (Colossians 3:1). What does it mean for me to seek the things above in my daily work?
She came up behind him and touched the fringe of his clothes (Luke 8:44). What need do I hide that I want to bring to Jesus?
Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace (Luke 8:48). Who needs to hear a word of welcome from me?
pm.resp: Lord, touch us and heal us.
interc: For all who are chronically ill, that they may find in Christ healing and peace.
For those who feel ashamed or excluded, that the Church may receive them as sons and daughters.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick, that they may serve with skill and compassion.
For all Christians who today honour the Body and Blood of Christ, that the Eucharist may unite us in faith and love.
For our parish, that we may set our hearts on the things above and do our work on earth with heavenly hope.
pm.close: Father, our life is hidden with Christ in you. Turn our hearts to the things that are above, let us touch your Son with faith in the Holy Mysteries, and send us out in his peace, until we are revealed with him in glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul, worried for the young church, sent Timothy to strengthen and encourage them, so that no one would be shaken by persecution.
He feared that the tempter would make their faith fail and his labour be in vain.
The poor widow gave two small coins, all she had to live on, and Jesus said she gave more than all the rich.
2027-05-28.action: Encourage one person today who is struggling in faith or in life.
2027-05-28.question: What would it look like for me to give God not my surplus but myself?

family.explain: Many rich people put a lot of money into the temple box. Then a poor widow came and put in two tiny coins. Nobody noticed her, but Jesus did. He said she gave more than everyone else, because the rich gave what they had left over, but she gave everything she had. God loves it when we give with our whole heart, even if the gift is small.
family.intention: We pray for poor families and for those who share even when they have little.
family.ask: Ask: “What small thing can each of us give this week with our whole heart?”

illus: An illustration

In a hamlet near Ranni, a widow who worked as a daily labourer used to bring a small bundle of rice to church each month for the parish poor box, a handful set aside from every day's cooking. The parish priest once told her gently that she need not bring it, since she herself had so little. She answered that she set the handful aside before she cooked, so that God would always get the first share and not the leftovers. When the parish later began a scheme to help families in need, the committee found that the first gift recorded in the old register was hers, a few kilos of rice, written down years before by a priest who had kept a note of what she gave.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you gave your whole life for us on the Cross. Make us generous like the poor widow and encouraging like Timothy. Amen.
share: We sent Timothy... to strengthen and encourage you for the sake of your faith (1 Thessalonians 3:2). Who has been a Timothy to me?
So that no one would be shaken by these persecutions (1 Thessalonians 3:3). What is shaking my faith at present?
She out of her poverty has put in everything she had (Mark 12:44). What is my two coins?
pm.resp: Lord, make us generous and faithful.
interc: For Christians who suffer persecution, that they may not be shaken but stand firm in faith.
For missionaries, catechists and all who are sent to strengthen others, that they may be faithful co-workers of God.
For widows and the poor, that they may be honoured and cared for in the Church.
For all who are tempted to give up, that someone may come to encourage them.
For our parish, that we may give generously from what we have and not only from what we can spare.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave everything on the Cross, and you saw the widow's two coins. Strengthen us in trials, make us encouragers of one another, and teach us to give ourselves with all we have. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul left Titus in Crete to appoint elders in every town; a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless and hold firm to the trustworthy word.
Jesus: no one who puts anything, even life itself, above him can be his disciple.
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow him cannot be his disciple; St Theodosia's name recalls the martyrs who loved Christ more than life.
2027-05-29.action: Pray today for vocations to the priesthood and religious life from your own parish.
2027-05-29.question: Is there anything I love more than Christ?

family.explain: Jesus said that to be his disciple we must love him even more than our family and our own life, and we must carry our cross and follow him. This does not mean we stop loving our parents or brothers and sisters. It means Jesus comes first, and when we put him first, we learn to love everyone better. Tomorrow is Vocations Day, when we pray for priests and sisters.
family.intention: We pray for our priests and for young people whom God is calling to serve him.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one cross each of us can carry for Jesus this week without complaining?”

illus: An illustration

A parish priest in a village near Kollam kept a small framed photograph of a family in his office: a farmer, his wife and their five children standing in front of a small house. When people asked about it, he said it was his own family, taken the year before he entered the seminary. He would point to the corner of the photo, where a calendar of saints hung on the wall behind them, and say: my father prayed the evening prayer under that calendar every night, even after the worst day in the field. I learned there what a steward of God looks like. I only took it to the altar.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, give your Church shepherds after your own heart, and teach us to carry our cross and follow you. Amen.
share: Appoint elders in every town (Titus 1:5). Which priest has shaped my faith, and have I thanked God for him?
He must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled (Titus 1:8). Which of these virtues do I most need?
Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). What is my cross at present?
pm.resp: Lord, send labourers into your harvest.
interc: For our bishops and priests, that they may be blameless stewards of God's household.
For young people whom God is calling to the priesthood and religious life, that they may answer with generosity.
For Christian families, that they may be the first seminary where vocations are born.
For those who suffer for their faith, that like the martyrs they may carry the cross with courage.
For our parish, that on Vocations Day tomorrow many may hear God's call.
pm.close: Father, you sent your apostles to appoint shepherds for your people. Give us bishops and priests after your own heart, make our homes places where vocations grow, and grant us to love your Son above all things and follow him with our cross. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: St Paul thanks God because the Thessalonians' faith is growing abundantly and their love for one another is increasing, even in persecution.
Jesus prays: Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you.
Eternal life is to know the only true God and Jesus Christ whom he sent; at the end of May we ask the Mother of God to teach us that knowing.
2027-05-31.action: Pray today in your own words, as a child speaks to a father, before saying any set prayer.
2027-05-31.question: Is my faith growing, and is my love for others increasing with it?

family.explain: On the night before he died, Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed to his Father. He said that eternal life means knowing God, not just knowing about him but knowing him like our best friend and our Father. Today is the last day of May, the month of Mary. Mary knew Jesus better than anyone, and she can help us to know him too.
family.intention: We pray that our family may know Jesus better and love one another more.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we get to know Jesus better as a family this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Chengannur, a boy preparing for his First Holy Communion was asked by the catechism teacher what he knew about God. He recited everything perfectly: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, the Creation, the commandments. Then she asked him a second question: do you know God? He was silent for a long time. That evening he asked his grandmother how a person can know God. She took him to the corner of the house where the family prayed, lit the lamp before the picture of the Mother of God holding her Son, and said: you start by talking to him every day, as you talk to me. That is how you came to know me.

pm.open: Father, this is eternal life: to know you and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. With the holy Mother of God, let us know your Son more deeply. Amen.
share: Your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing (2 Thessalonians 1:3). Where have I seen faith and love grow together?
Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son (John 17:1). What does the glory of the Cross mean to me?
This is eternal life, that they may know you (John 17:3). How do I come to know God more deeply?
pm.resp: Lord, let us know you and love you.
interc: For the Church, that her faith may grow abundantly and her love increase, especially where she suffers persecution.
For all who know about God but have not yet met him, that they may come to know him as Father.
For mothers, that like the holy Mother of God they may carry Christ to their children.
For the afflicted, that God may give them relief and strengthen their steadfastness.
For our parish, as the month of Mary ends, that we may grow in the knowledge and love of Jesus Christ.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son to give us eternal life. Let us know you and the one whom you have sent, let our faith and love grow together, and with the holy Mother of God let us carry Christ to others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, at the Last Supper Jesus told his friends: “A little while, and you will no longer see me; and again a little while, and you will see me.” They did not understand. He explained with a picture every mother knows: a woman in labour has pain, but when the child is born she forgets the pain for joy.

That is Easter. The Cross was the labour pain; the Resurrection is the birth of new life. And Jesus promised: “I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.” Christian joy is not the absence of trouble. It is a joy that rests on the risen Christ, and so no one can take it away.

In Acts the disciples are thrown out of a city, and yet they are “filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.” Jesus also promises the Spirit of truth to guide us, and invites us to ask in his name, “so that your joy may be complete”. On Thursday we celebrate his Ascension; then we wait for the Spirit.

St Paul tells us how this joy shows: “Seek the things that are above.” Put off anger, lies and impurity; put on compassion and love. As Proverbs says, “love covers all offences.” Let us live this week as people whose joy no one can take away. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told his friends: “You will be sad for a little while, but then you will be very happy!”
They were sad when Jesus died, but so happy when they saw him alive again! Jesus said nobody can take that joy away.
When you feel sad, remember Jesus is alive and loves you. Let's say: “Jesus, you are my joy!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, forty days after Easter Jesus leads his disciples out to Bethany. He lifts up his hands and blesses them, and while he is blessing them he is carried up into heaven. The last picture the disciples have of Jesus is of hands raised in blessing. He has never lowered them.

The Ascension does not mean that Jesus has gone far away. It means that our human nature, which he took from Mary, now sits at the right hand of the Father. Where he, our Head, has gone, we, his body, hope to follow. Heaven is our home.

But the angels say: “Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” The Ascension is not a time for gazing at the sky; it is a time for mission. Jesus said: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news.” And they went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them.

Elijah was taken up, and Elisha received his mantle and his spirit. Jesus ascends, and he will send his Spirit upon us at Pentecost. Like the apostles with Mary, let us spend these ten days in prayer: Come, Holy Spirit. And at every Qurbono, when we hear “Lift up your hearts,” let us truly lift them up to him. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus went up to heaven! He took his friends to a hill, raised his hands and blessed them, and then went up into the sky until a cloud hid him.
Jesus is now with God the Father, but he still blesses us and loves us. And he promised to send the Holy Spirit to help us.
For the next ten days, let's pray every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

intro: Saint Paul reads the Ascension through Psalm 68: the King goes up in triumph and gives gifts to his people. Those gifts build up the Church.

sub: The King goes up in triumph.
Sin and death defeated.
The victor shares the spoils.
points.apply: Thank Christ today for his victory over your sins.

sub: Apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors, teachers.
Bezalel filled with the spirit to build the tabernacle.
Every gift for the common good.
points.apply: Ask yourself what gift God has given you, and offer it to your parish.

sub: No longer children tossed about.
Speaking the truth in love.
The whole body growing together.
points.apply: Learn one teaching of the faith more deeply this month.

concl: The ascended Christ is not absent: he pours out gifts to build up his body.
We grow toward him, our Head, by using those gifts in love.
opts.resolve: In these days before Pentecost I will discover and offer my gift for building up the Church.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this feast of Suloko Saint Paul helps us to see the Ascension in a new way. He quotes an old psalm of victory: when he ascended on high he made captivity itself a captive; he gave gifts to his people (Ephesians 4:8; Psalm 68:18). The picture is of a king returning from battle, leading his defeated enemies behind him and sharing the spoils with his people.

Christ has fought the great battle. On the Cross and in the Resurrection he defeated sin and death. Today he goes up to the Father as victor. But he does not keep the victory for himself. He gives gifts. Paul names them: the gifts he gave were that some would be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors and teachers, to equip the saints for the work of ministry, for building up the body of Christ (Ephesians 4:11–12).

In the book of Exodus, when the tabernacle was to be built, God said of the craftsman Bezalel: I have filled him with divine spirit, with ability, intelligence, and knowledge in every kind of craft (Exodus 31:3). God gave skills so that his dwelling could be built. So too the ascended Christ gives gifts so that his Church may be built: bishops and priests, catechists and singers, parents and teachers, those who care for the sick and those who pray in hidden ways.

What is the purpose of all these gifts? That we may grow. Paul says we must no longer be children, tossed to and fro and blown about by every wind of doctrine, but speaking the truth in love, we must grow up in every way into him who is the head, into Christ (Ephesians 4:14–15). Hosea shows God teaching Israel to walk, holding them by the arms (Hosea 11:3). The ascended Lord still holds us and teaches us to walk.

In these ten days before Pentecost, let us ask: what gift has the Lord given me, and am I using it for his body? Let us offer it to our parish. Let us learn our faith more deeply, so that we are not tossed about. And at every Holy Qurbono let us lift up our hearts to Christ our Head, who has gone up to give gifts to his people. Amen.

opts.a: Our High Priest in the true sanctuary
intro: The Ascension is not only a departure. Christ enters heaven itself as our High Priest, carrying our names before the Father and writing his law on our hearts.

sub: Not a sanctuary made by hands.
He appears before God for us.
Our human nature at the Father's right hand.
points.apply: At the Holy Qurbono, when the priest calls us to lift up our minds and hearts on high, lift them to Christ.

sub: Aaron carried the names of Israel on his heart.
Christ carries ours.
Never alone in prayer.
points.apply: Bring the names of those you love to Christ in prayer each day.

sub: The tablets placed in the ark.
The new covenant promised.
The Spirit who writes within.
points.apply: Pray each day of the ten days: Holy Spirit, write God's law on my heart.

concl: The ascended Christ is our High Priest in heaven, interceding for us always.
From there he sends the Spirit to write his law on our hearts.
opts.resolve: In these days before Pentecost I will pray each day for those I love, trusting that Christ intercedes for them, and ask the Spirit to write his law in my heart.
homily: Dear friends, the Ascension can sound like a farewell. But the Letter to the Hebrews shows us that it is an entrance. Once a year the high priest of Israel passed through the curtain into the Holy of Holies with the blood of the offering (Leviticus 16:15). Today Christ, our High Priest, enters a greater sanctuary: Christ did not enter a sanctuary made by human hands, a mere copy of the true one, but he entered into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf (Hebrews 9:24).

On our behalf. That is the heart of today's feast. Our Lord takes our human nature, the body he received from Mary, the body that bore the wounds of the Cross, into the presence of the Father. Where our Head has gone, we his members hope to follow.

And what does he do there? When Aaron went into the holy place, he carried on his breast the names of the twelve tribes: so Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on his heart (Exodus 28:29). Christ carries our names on his heart. He always lives to make intercession for them (Hebrews 7:25). When we pray, we never pray alone. The ascended Lord is already praying for us.

One of today's readings tells how Moses placed the tablets of the law in the ark (Deuteronomy 10:5). Another gives God's promise through Jeremiah: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts (Jeremiah 31:33). From heaven the ascended Christ will send his Spirit to do exactly this. Saint Paul says that we are a letter written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3).

So in these ten days of waiting, let us pray each day for those we love, trusting that Christ carries their names before the Father. Let us ask: Holy Spirit, write God's law on my heart. And at every Holy Qurbono, when we are called to lift up our minds and hearts on high, let us lift them to where our High Priest is. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, we are living the days between the Ascension and Pentecost. Jesus has gone to the Father; the Spirit has not yet come. And what did the apostles do? They went to the upper room and “devoted themselves to prayer, together with Mary the mother of Jesus.”

Jesus had said something surprising: “It is to your advantage that I go away.” How can it be better that Jesus goes? Because when he was on earth he could be in one place at a time. The Spirit makes him present everywhere: in every heart, in every family, on every altar. The Spirit will convict the world of sin, of righteousness and of judgment.

In the evening Gospel Jesus prays: “Father, the hour has come… This is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.” He is still praying for us at the right hand of the Father.

And God says to us what he said to Joshua: “Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened, for the Lord your God is with you wherever you go.” This week let us do what the apostles did: pray with Mary, every day, “Come, Holy Spirit.” Amen.
kids: Children, after Jesus went back to heaven, his friends waited in a room in Jerusalem. What were they doing? Praying, together with Mary!
Jesus had promised to send the Holy Spirit to help them. Next Sunday we will celebrate when the Spirit came!
This week, let's pray with Mary every day: “Come, Holy Spirit!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is the birthday of the Church. Fifty days after Easter, the apostles were gathered in prayer with Mary. Suddenly there came a sound like a mighty wind, and tongues like fire rested on each of them. They were filled with the Holy Spirit, and the frightened men who had locked the doors went out into the streets and proclaimed Christ.

People from every nation heard them, each in his own language, speaking of the wonders of God. At Babel, pride had scattered humanity into many languages that could not understand one another. At Pentecost the Spirit gathers the nations into one faith, without erasing their languages. That is why we can pray the Holy Qurbono in Syriac and Malayalam, in Tamil and Hindi and English: one Spirit, many tongues.

Moses once said: “Would that all the Lord's people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!” Ezekiel promised: “A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you.” Today it happens. And it happened to you on the day of your Baptism, when you were anointed with holy Myron. The Spirit is not only for bishops and saints; he lives in you.

St Paul says the one Spirit gives many gifts, each for the common good. What is your gift? Music, teaching, caring for the sick, organising, praying? Offer it. And let us pray today with the whole Church: Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful, and kindle in us the fire of your love. Amen.
kids: Children, happy birthday to the Church! Today the Holy Spirit came on the apostles like a big wind and little flames of fire!
The apostles were afraid before, but the Spirit made them brave, and they told everyone about Jesus in many languages.
The same Holy Spirit came to you at your baptism. He helps you to be brave and kind. Let's pray: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart!”

opts.a: Another Advocate, who teaches and reminds
intro: In the Gospel Jesus promises another Advocate who will abide with us, be in us, teach us everything and remind us of all he said. Pentecost is the fulfilment of that promise.

sub: If you love me.
Keeping the commandments is love.
The Father and the Son make their home with us.
points.apply: Keep one commandment this week with special care as an act of love.

sub: Another Advocate.
He abides with you, and he will be in you.
God's Spirit placed within us.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Holy Spirit, dwell in me today.

sub: The Spirit teaches everything.
He reminds us of Jesus' words.
He comes down on the gifts at the Holy Qurbono.
points.apply: Before reading the Gospel each day, ask the Holy Spirit to teach you.

concl: The Holy Spirit is not a distant power but the Advocate who lives within us.
He teaches us, reminds us of Christ's words, and makes Christ present in the Holy Qurbono.
opts.resolve: This week I will begin each day by asking the Holy Spirit to dwell in me and teach me through the Gospel.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on this feast of Pentecost the Gospel takes us back to the upper room on the night before Jesus died. He promised: I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Advocate, to be with you forever (John 14:16). An advocate is one who stands beside us, defends us, encourages us. Jesus had been that for his disciples. Now he promises another, the Holy Spirit.

Notice where the Spirit will be. Jesus says: you know him, because he abides with you, and he will be in you (John 14:17). Ezekiel had heard God say: I will put my spirit within you (Ezekiel 36:27). The Spirit is not only above us or around us. He lives within the baptised. That is why Jesus speaks of love: if you love me, you will keep my commandments (John 14:15). Those who love me will keep my word, and my Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them (John 14:23).

And what does the Spirit do? The Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you (John 14:26). On the day of Pentecost the apostles suddenly understood what Jesus had taught them. Isaiah had foretold the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might (Isaiah 11:2). The Spirit is the Church's living memory of Jesus.

We meet the Spirit at the heart of every Holy Qurbono. The priest calls upon the Holy Spirit to come down upon the bread and wine, and by his power they become the Body and Blood of Christ. The same Spirit who came upon the apostles comes upon our altar and upon us, to make us one body in Christ.

So let us welcome the Advocate today. Each morning this week, let us pray: Holy Spirit, dwell in me today. Before we read the Gospel, let us ask him to teach us. And let us keep the word of Jesus out of love, so that the Father and the Son may make their home in us. Come, Holy Spirit. Amen.

opts.a: The Spirit on the seventy and on Saul
intro: Two of today's readings show the Spirit coming upon the seventy elders and upon Saul. One story shows the Spirit shared; the other warns that the Spirit can be grieved and refused.

sub: Moses could not carry the people alone.
The Spirit placed on the seventy.
Poured out on all flesh.
points.apply: Share the burden of your parish: offer help to your priest or a parish group.

sub: God gave Saul another heart.
The Spirit changes us from within.
The fruit of the Spirit.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit to ask for and practise this week.

sub: Saul's later disobedience.
The Spirit departed from him.
Repentance keeps the door open.
points.apply: Make a good confession soon if you have grieved the Spirit by serious sin.

concl: God shares his Spirit with all his people and gives us new hearts.
We must guard that gift and never grieve the Spirit by unrepented sin.
opts.resolve: This week I will ask for one fruit of the Spirit, share the burden of my parish, and guard the gift of the Spirit by confession.
homily: Dear friends, among today's readings are two old stories about the Spirit of God. In the first, Moses is exhausted. He cannot carry the whole people alone. So the Lord came down in the cloud and spoke to him, and took some of the spirit that was on him and put it on the seventy elders (Numbers 11:25). God shares his Spirit so that the burden is shared.

At Pentecost that sharing reaches everyone. Saint Peter stands up and quotes the prophet Joel: I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy (Acts 2:17). Not only the seventy, not only the apostles, but every baptised person receives the Spirit. Each of us is called to carry part of the Church's burden: in our families, in our parishes, in our work.

The second story is about Saul. When Samuel anointed him, God gave him another heart, and the spirit of God possessed him (1 Samuel 10:9–10). That is what the Spirit does: he changes the heart from within. Saint Paul describes the new heart: the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control (Galatians 5:22–23).

But Saul's story has a sad ending. Through pride and disobedience he turned away from God, and later we read: the spirit of the Lord departed from Saul (1 Samuel 16:14). This is a serious warning. The gift of the Spirit can be refused by serious sin that we do not repent of. Saint Paul says: do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God, with which you were marked with a seal for the day of redemption (Ephesians 4:30). And David, after his sin, prayed: do not take your holy spirit from me (Psalm 51:11). David repented, and God restored him.

So on this Pentecost let us thank God for the Spirit given to us in Baptism and Myron. Let us share the burden of our parish. Let us ask for one fruit of the Spirit this week and practise it. And if we have grieved the Spirit, let us not wait: a good confession opens the door again. Come, Holy Spirit, and never leave us. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, last Sunday we celebrated Pentecost, the coming of the Holy Spirit. Today we ask: what difference does the Spirit make? St Paul answers: the Spirit bears fruit. “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.” Read that list slowly; it is a portrait of Jesus, and of what he wants to grow in us.

In the evening Gospel Jesus tells of a sower. Some seed falls on the path, some on rock, some among thorns, and some on good soil. The seed is the same; the soil makes the difference. The good soil is “an honest and good heart” that hears the Word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience. The Spirit keeps sowing; are we good soil?

In John's Gospel the crowds look for Jesus because he gave them bread. He tells them: “Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life.” And he says: “The bread of God is that which comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.” That bread is given to us at this altar.

Today is also a day to pray for vocations. Jeremiah says: “I know the plans I have for you, plans for your welfare, to give you a future with hope.” God has a plan for every young person here: priesthood, religious life, marriage, a mission. Let us ask the Spirit to show it, and let us choose this week one fruit of the Spirit to practise. Amen.
kids: Children, when a tree is healthy, it gives fruit. When the Holy Spirit lives in us, we give fruit too: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness!
Jesus told a story about a farmer sowing seed. The seed that fell on good soil grew a big harvest. Our hearts should be good soil for God's Word.
Which fruit will you grow this week? Kindness? Patience? Let's say: “Holy Spirit, help me grow good fruit!”

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, on the day of Pentecost Peter stood up and said: this is what the prophet Joel foretold: “I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh… everyone who calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.” Not only on priests and prophets, but on sons and daughters, old and young. On you.

And what does the Spirit do in us? St Paul says: “There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. The law of the Spirit of life has set you free.” The same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead lives in us and will raise our mortal bodies. We are not slaves of sin; we are temples of the Spirit.

In the Gospel Jesus prays all night, chooses the Twelve, and then looks at his disciples and says: Blessed are you who are poor, blessed are you who are hungry, blessed are you who weep. This is the strange happiness of the Spirit: not the happiness of the rich and comfortable, but of those who trust God.

God says in Leviticus: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.” Holiness is not only for saints in pictures. Jesus shows two ways: to take up the cross and follow him, and to give a cup of cold water to a little one in his name. Big crosses and small kindnesses. Let us do one hidden act of kindness each day this week. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus once prayed all night long! And in the morning he chose twelve friends to be his apostles.
Then he said: “Happy are the poor, happy are the hungry, happy are those who cry, because God will take care of them.”
Jesus also said that even giving a cup of water in his name is precious. What kind thing can you do today?

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today is May Day, Labour Day, and our Church remembers Mar Yauseph, Patron of Workers. In the Gospel the people of Nazareth say of Jesus: is not this the carpenter's son? (Matthew 13:55). They meant to belittle him. But think of it: the Son of God was known in his own town by the work of his foster father. For most of his life on earth he worked with his hands.

St Paul says to the Thessalonians: we were not idle when we were with you; we worked night and day so as not to burden anyone (2 Thessalonians 3:7–8). And he gave them a rule: anyone unwilling to work should not eat. Honest work is not a curse; God gave the first man a garden to till and keep. Work done well and offered to God becomes holy.

The Panchangam also remembers Jeremiah the Prophet. Like Jesus, he was not honoured in his own town. God sent him to a potter's house and showed him the clay on the wheel: so are you in my hand, O house of Israel (Jeremiah 18:6). God shapes us in our ordinary work, in our patience, in our honesty when no one is watching.

So today let us offer our work to God. Let us pray for workers who are underpaid, for those who have no job, for those far from home earning for their families. And let us ask Mar Yauseph to teach us to work quietly, faithfully and for the love of Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today is Labour Day. Do you know what job St Joseph did? He was a carpenter! He made tables and doors, and Jesus helped him in the workshop. People in Nazareth said, “Isn't he the carpenter's son?” Jesus did ordinary work, just like your parents do. When you do your homework neatly, or help to sweep the house without grumbling, you can say, “Jesus, this is for you!” Then your work becomes a prayer.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! St Paul begs the Corinthians: do not accept the grace of God in vain. Then he says: see, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! (2 Corinthians 6:1–2). We like to put God's time in the past or the future. Paul puts it here: today, this Monday, with all its ordinary work.

Paul describes his life as an apostle: afflictions, hardships, beatings, sleepless nights, hunger. And yet he says: as sorrowful, yet always rejoicing; as poor, yet making many rich; as having nothing, and yet possessing everything (2 Corinthians 6:10). Only someone who has Christ can say that. Having him, he has everything.

In the Gospel Jesus says: I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me will never walk in darkness but will have the light of life (John 8:12). He is not one light among many; he is the light by which we see everything else. And his witness is true, because the Father who sent him testifies to him.

In three days we celebrate Suloko, the Ascension, and then we wait for the Holy Spirit. Let us not wait for a better time to turn to God. Today let us do the good we have been postponing, and let us walk in his light. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever been in a room when the lights suddenly went off? It is hard to find the door, and you might bump into a chair. Jesus says: “I am the light of the world.” When we follow Jesus, we do not get lost. St Paul also says something important: “Now is the time!” Don't wait until tomorrow to say sorry or to help someone. Do it today, and Jesus' light will shine through you.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! St Paul remembers his short time in Thessalonica. He had been mistreated at Philippi, yet he says: we had courage in our God to declare to you the gospel of God (1 Thessalonians 2:2). And his motive was pure: not to please mortals, but to please God who tests our hearts (2:4).

Then he uses two tender pictures. We were gentle among you, like a nurse tenderly caring for her own children. And: we dealt with each one of you like a father with his children (2:7, 11). He adds: we were determined to share with you not only the gospel of God but also our own selves (2:8). The Gospel is passed on not only by words but by lives given.

In the Gospel some of Jesus' hearers insult him: you are a Samaritan and have a demon. Jesus does not insult them back. He says: I honor my Father. And he gives a great promise: whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). The one who says this has already risen from the dead.

So let us keep his word, and let us share it as Paul did, with our time and our love. Parents, teachers, priests: be gentle and firm, and give yourselves. And let us all remember: in Christ, death is not the end. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Who takes care of you when you are sick? Maybe your mother or your grandmother sits beside you and gives you medicine and soup. St Paul says he loved the people of Thessalonica like that, as gently as a nurse with little children. He gave them his time and his whole heart. Jesus says that if we keep his word, we will live for ever with him. Let us keep Jesus' words and share his love gently with everyone.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Tomorrow is Suloko. Tonight St Paul asks us for something simple: pray for us, so that the word of the Lord may spread rapidly and be glorified everywhere (2 Thessalonians 3:1). The apostle needed the prayer of ordinary believers. Our priests and missionaries need ours.

Paul knew that not all have faith. But he says: the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one (3:3). And he blesses them: may the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the steadfastness of Christ (3:5). God himself clears the road for our hearts.

In the Gospel Jesus says: your eye is the lamp of your body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body is full of light (Luke 11:34). What we look at shapes who we become. A lamp is not hidden in a cellar; it is put on a stand so that all may see.
Tomorrow we will lift our eyes to the ascending Lord. Let us prepare tonight: pray for those who preach, trust the faithful Lord, and keep our eyes clear and our lives full of light. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! At home, when your family lights the evening lamp, where do you put it? In the middle, where everyone can see. Jesus says our eyes are like a lamp. When we look at good things, like the beautiful world God made or kind people, our hearts fill with light. Tomorrow we celebrate Jesus going up to heaven. Tonight, say a little prayer for your priest, so that he can tell many people about Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Yesterday we celebrated Suloko, the Ascension. Today the Panchangam keeps the Finding of the Cross of our Lord. The one who has gone up to the Father is the Crucified; the Cross was the road of his glory. Very early, by the time of St Cyril of Jerusalem around 350, pieces of the wood of the Cross were honoured throughout the world, and tradition tells that St Helena found it on Golgotha.

St Paul writes in large letters with his own hand: may I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by which the world has been crucified to me, and I to the world (Galatians 6:14). What matters is not outward marks but a new creation. Paul carried the marks of Jesus on his body; he was not ashamed of them.

In the Gospel Jesus says that the kingdom is like a treasure hidden in a field. A man finds it and in his joy sells everything to buy the field (Matthew 13:44). The Cross is that treasure. The world sees loss; the believer sees the love of God, and gladly gives up everything for it.

Today is also First Friday. We honour the Heart of Jesus, opened on the Cross, from which blood and water flowed. Let us make the sign of the Cross with love, go to confession, receive the Holy Qurbono, and in these days of waiting ask the Spirit to make us boast only of the Cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you like stories about hidden treasure? Jesus told one: a man found treasure buried in a field and was so happy that he sold everything to buy that field. Today we remember the day the Cross of Jesus was found. The Cross is our treasure, because it shows how much Jesus loves us. Every time you make the sign of the Cross, do it slowly and say in your heart: “Jesus, thank you for loving me!”

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today the Panchangam remembers Mar Yohannan Shleeha, St John the Apostle, whom tradition knows as the disciple whom Jesus loved. He leaned on the Lord's breast at the Supper, he stood at the Cross, and he was the first to recognise the risen Lord on the shore.

In the Gospel Peter sees John and asks: Lord, what about him? Jesus answers: if it is my will that he remain until I come, what is that to you? Follow me! (John 21:21–22). We are not to compare our road with another's. Each of us has one task: to follow Jesus.

St Paul asks: who will separate us from the love of Christ? Hardship, distress, persecution, famine, sword? No, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us (Romans 8:35, 37). John lived this. In his old age, St Jerome tells us, he would say only: little children, love one another.

From the Cross Jesus gave his Mother to John, and John took her into his home. Today we also thank God for the Daughters of Mary, founded on this day in 1938, who serve the poor in the name of Mary. Let us take Mary into our homes, and with her wait in prayer for the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Today we remember St John. He was one of Jesus' best friends! At the Last Supper he sat right next to Jesus.
