On Good Friday, when many friends ran away, John stayed near the Cross with Mother Mary. Jesus said to him, “Here is your mother,” and John took care of her. When John was very old, he kept saying, “Little children, love one another.” Let us say it too, and do it!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! We are living in the ten days between Suloko and Pentecost. The apostles are in the upper room, waiting and praying, and today our Church remembers one of them: Mar Shemun Shleeha, St Simon the Zealot. We know little about his life, but his name tells us something important. He was a man of zeal, a man with fire in his heart. Before he met Jesus, that fire may have burned against the Romans and against anyone who served them. After he met Jesus, it burned for the Kingdom of God.

In the Gospel we meet the very kind of man a zealot would have despised: Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector, rich from other people's money. The crowd blocked his way, so he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree. And Jesus stopped. He looked up and said, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down; for I must stay at your house today.” Notice: Jesus did not wait for Zacchaeus to become good before he came to his house. He came first, and his coming made Zacchaeus good. The man who had taken now began to give: half of his possessions to the poor, and four times back to anyone he had cheated.

Now picture the table of the Twelve. Simon the Zealot on one side, Matthew the former tax collector on the other. In the world they would have been enemies. At the table of Jesus they were brothers. This is what the Holy Spirit will do at Pentecost: not take away our zeal, but purify it. The anger goes; the fire stays. St Paul, waiting in Ephesus “until Pentecost,” shows us what purified zeal looks like. He sees a wide door and many adversaries, and he is not afraid. He tells the Corinthians to protect young Timothy and to let Apollos come in his own time. That is zeal with patience, zeal with gentleness.

So in these days of waiting, let us ask ourselves: is there a Zacchaeus in my life, someone I have written off? Let us pray for that person by name until Pentecost. And let us let Jesus say to us too, “I must stay at your house today.” He will say it at this altar, when he comes to us in his Body and Blood. Let us hurry down and welcome him with joy.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever climbed a tree to see something far away? In today's Gospel a short man named Zacchaeus climbed a tree to see Jesus, because the crowd was too big. Nobody liked Zacchaeus, because he took too much money from people. But Jesus stopped right under the tree, looked up and called him by his name! Jesus went to his house, and Zacchaeus was so happy that he decided to give money to the poor and pay back everyone he had cheated. Today we also remember St Simon, one of Jesus' twelve friends. He had a fiery heart, and Jesus taught him to use that fire for love. This week, be kind to someone others leave out. That is what Jesus did.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! In the Gospel today Jesus does something before he chooses his apostles: he prays. He goes up the mountain and spends the whole night in prayer to God. Only when day comes does he call the Twelve by name. Before every great step, Jesus speaks with his Father. If the Son of God prayed through the night before choosing, how much more do we need prayer before our choices of life, of work, of marriage, of vocation.

Today the Panchangam reminds us of two brothers who were chosen for a great mission: Sts Cyril and Methodius. More than a thousand years ago they were sent to the Slav peoples, who had no written language. Cyril made an alphabet for them, and the brothers translated the Gospels and the Liturgy, so that the people could pray to God in their own words. Some people opposed them and said God should be praised only in three great languages. But the Pope welcomed them and blessed their work. They knew that the Holy Spirit does not make every people the same; he makes every people holy.

St Paul tells the Ephesians the great plan of God: “to gather up all things in him, things in heaven and things on earth.” Christ gathers. He brings together Jews and Greeks, Slavs and Syrians, Keralites and people of every state of India, and makes of them one Body. And the seal of this gathering is the Holy Spirit. St Paul says that when we heard the Gospel and believed, we “were marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit.” We received that seal at our Baptism and Holy Mooron. In five days, at Pentecost, the Church will celebrate the day when the apostles spoke and everyone heard God's wonders in his own language.

So let us ask ourselves today: do I value the prayers of my Church? Do I teach them to my children? Our fathers prayed the Holy Qurbono in Syriac; today we pray it in Malayalam and in many other languages, and it is the same holy sacrifice. Let us love it, learn it and hand it on. And let us pray for all who carry the Gospel to new peoples, that like Cyril and Methodius they may give others the words of life.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you know how many languages there are in India? Hundreds! Malayalam, Tamil, Hindi, English and so many more. Long ago two brothers named Cyril and Methodius went to a land where people spoke a language that had never been written down. So Cyril made up new letters, a whole new alphabet! Then they wrote the stories of Jesus in that language. Imagine how happy the people were to hear about Jesus in their own words. Jesus wants everybody to know that he loves them. In today's Gospel he prayed all night and then chose twelve friends to help him. This week, learn one new prayer by heart and teach it to a younger brother, sister or cousin.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! In these days between the Ascension and Pentecost, the Church remembers two bishops who lived more than sixteen hundred years ago: Mar Yaqob of Nisibis and Mar Epiphanios of Cyprus. Mar Yaqob was one of the bishops at the great Council of Nicaea, which gave us the words we still say in the Creed: that the Son is of one being with the Father. Mar Epiphanios spent his life defending that same faith. One thing he taught is very useful for us today. Some people in his time denied the honour of the Mother of God; others went too far and worshipped her like a goddess. Epiphanios said: honour Mary, but worship only the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. That is exactly what the Church still teaches.

St Paul gives us today a beautiful sentence: “work out your own salvation with fear and trembling; for it is God who is at work in you, enabling you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.” Sometimes we think that either God does everything, or we must do everything. Paul says: God is at work in you, so you work too. Every good desire you have is already his gift. Every good deed is his grace and your effort together.

Then Paul asks us to do everything “without murmuring and arguing,” so that we may “shine like stars in the world.” Think how much murmuring there is in our homes and workplaces: about the weather, the prices, the neighbours, the parish. A star does not complain about the darkness. It shines. In the Gospel, Jesus says that people know how to read the clouds and the wind, but do not know how to read the present time. In May we all watch for the monsoon. Jesus asks us to watch for something greater: the coming of the Holy Spirit.

And Jesus gives one practical command. If you are on the way to court with your accuser, settle the case on the way. We are all on the way. Is there someone I have not spoken to for a long time? Someone I have hurt? Before Pentecost, let us make peace. The Spirit loves to come into hearts that have forgiven. Then at this altar, when we receive the Body and Blood of the Lord, we shall be ready to shine.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! In May, when the sky gets dark over the hills and the wind starts to blow, what do we say? “The rain is coming!” Jesus says that people are very good at watching the clouds. But he wants us to watch for something even more wonderful. Right now the Church is waiting for the Holy Spirit, who will come at Pentecost on Sunday. How can we get ready? St Paul says: do everything without grumbling. And Jesus says: make peace with anyone you have quarrelled with. So this week, if you have fought with a brother, a sister or a friend, say sorry first. Then your heart will be ready for the Holy Spirit, like a field ready for the rain.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! In today's Gospel Jesus stands up in the Temple on the last great day of the feast of Tabernacles and cries out with a loud voice: “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink.” Every day of that feast the priests poured water at the altar and prayed for rain. And Jesus says: I am the source. St John tells us what he meant: “he said this about the Spirit,” who would be given once Jesus was glorified.

Now Jesus has been glorified. He has suffered, died and risen, and a week ago, on Suloko, we celebrated his Ascension. In three days, at Pentecost, the Spirit will be poured out. So these days are days of thirst. A person who is not thirsty does not look for water. Let us ask the Lord to make us thirsty for him: thirsty for prayer, for his word, for the Holy Qurbono, for holiness. Mar Ishaq Malpan of Antioch, whom we remember today, wrote long poems to help the faithful pray. He knew that the soul must learn to thirst.

The Letter to the Hebrews gives us something for the journey: hope. God made a promise to Abraham and swore by his own name, because there was no one greater. Abraham waited patiently and received what was promised. Then the letter says: “We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” Think of a boat in a storm. If its anchor holds, it will not be thrown onto the rocks. Our anchor is not thrown down into the sea but up into heaven, “behind the curtain,” where Jesus has gone before us as our forerunner and high priest.

So whatever storm you are in today, illness, money troubles, worry for your children, hold on to the anchor. Christ is at the Father's right hand, praying for you. And when the curtain of the sanctuary opens in the Holy Qurbono, remember that our hope has already entered there. Let us come to this altar thirsty, and the Lord will give us to drink.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! When you have been playing outside on a hot day, what do you want most? A glass of cold water! Jesus said, “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me.” He was talking about a different kind of thirst, a thirst in our hearts for God, for love, for goodness. And he promised to give us the Holy Spirit, like a river of water flowing inside us. This Sunday is Pentecost, when the Holy Spirit came. Today, every time you drink water, say a tiny prayer: “Jesus, fill me with your Spirit.” Then you will be ready for Sunday!

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Today our Church celebrates Mar Addai Shleeha, the apostle of Edessa. An old story, told by the historian Eusebius, says that the king of Edessa, Abgar, was very ill and sent a letter to Jesus asking him to come and heal him. After the Ascension of the Lord, the apostle Thomas sent Addai, one of the seventy disciples, to Edessa. Addai healed the king and preached the Gospel, and Edessa became one of the first Christian cities in the world. From there the faith spread to the Syriac-speaking peoples. That is why this feast matters to us: we too belong to the family of the Syriac Churches, and we too received the faith from the apostle Thomas.

Notice when Addai was sent: after the Ascension. The Lord had gone up to heaven, and his disciples went out to the ends of the earth. In the Gospel today Jesus tells them not to be afraid: “do not fear those who kill the body, and after that can do nothing more.” Many of the apostles did die for Christ. But Jesus gives them a reason for courage. God does not forget even a sparrow, a little bird sold for a few coins. “But even the hairs of your head are all counted. Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.”

St Paul, writing from prison, shows us another part of mission. He thanks the Philippians for sending him help. He says, “I have learned to be content with whatever I have,” and then the famous words, “I can do all things through him who strengthens me.” Paul is not boasting of his own strength. He is saying that Christ is his strength in hunger and in plenty. And he thanks them because they “shared his distress.” They could not travel with him, but by their prayer and their gifts they were part of his mission.

So today we are asked two things. First, to speak of Jesus without fear in our own place: our home, our office, our school. Second, to share in the work of those who go further: our missionary priests and sisters in North India and abroad. Pray for them, write to them, support them. In two days the Holy Spirit will come at Pentecost to give us courage. Let us receive the Lord in this Holy Qurbono and ask him to make us apostles like Mar Addai.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Have you ever watched little sparrows hopping around looking for grains of rice? They are small and seem unimportant. But Jesus said that God never forgets even one sparrow. And then he said something amazing: God has counted every hair on your head! Can you count your hair? No one can! But God knows you that well. So Jesus says, “Do not be afraid.” Today we remember Mar Addai, who travelled far away to tell a sick king about Jesus. He was not afraid, because he knew God loved him. When you feel scared, remember the sparrows, and say, “Jesus, I trust in you.”

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Tomorrow is Pentecost. Today, the last day of waiting, our Church turns to the Mother of God, and she does it in a very homely way: the Panchangam calls today the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God “for the ears of grain.” In May the wheat in the old Syriac lands was coming to the ear, and the Church brought the harvest to Mary and asked her prayers. Why Mary? Because the Fathers called her the field that was never sown, from which came the Bread of life. Jesus was born in Bethlehem, which means “house of bread,” and he feeds us with his own Body at every Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel a woman praises Jesus' Mother: “Blessed is the womb that bore you!” And Jesus says, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!” Is Jesus putting his Mother down? Not at all. He is telling us the secret of her greatness. Mary was blessed because she heard God's word and said yes to it: “let it be with me according to your word.” She kept the words of God in her heart and pondered them. So we too can share her blessedness, if we hear God's word and keep it.

St Paul gives us the farmer's lesson: “the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully... for God loves a cheerful giver.” Today we also remember Mar Pachomios, St Pachomius of Egypt. As a young soldier in prison, he was given bread by strangers in the night. They were Christians. That one act of kindness made him a Christian, and later he founded great communities of monks who prayed, worked and shared everything. We also pray today for Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios, whose name day it is.

So, on the eve of Pentecost, let us do three things. Let us thank God for the harvest and pray for our farmers. Let us give something today, cheerfully, to someone in need. And let us wait with Mary, as the apostles did, for the Holy Spirit. Let us say tonight, with the Mother of God, “Here am I; let it be with me according to your word.” Then tomorrow the Spirit will find a field ready for his harvest.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you know where bread comes from? From wheat, a plant that grows in fields. In May the wheat grows little heads full of grain, called ears. Today our Church thanks God for the grain, and remembers Mother Mary. Why? Because Mary gave us Jesus, who said, “I am the bread of life.” Jesus also said that the people who are really happy are those who listen to God's word and do it. Mary did that perfectly. Tomorrow is Pentecost, the birthday of the Church! Tonight, say a prayer with your family: “Mother Mary, help us to listen to Jesus. Come, Holy Spirit!”

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we kept Pentecost, and today a new season begins in our Church: the season of Pentecost. The days of waiting are over. The Spirit has come, and now the Church is sent out. St Paul tells us how to live in this season: only, live your life in a manner worthy of the gospel of Christ (Philippians 1:27).

Philippi was proud of being a Roman city. Paul tells its Christians that their true citizenship is in Christ's kingdom. He wants to hear that they are standing firm in one spirit, striving side by side with one mind for the faith of the gospel, and are in no way intimidated by your opponents (Philippians 1:27–28). Side by side, not each one alone; firm, not frightened.

In the Gospel Jesus sends the Twelve: proclaim the good news, cure the sick, cleanse the lepers. You received without payment; give without payment (Matthew 10:8). He sends them with nothing in their belts, so that everyone can see that the power is his and not theirs. They are to bring peace into every house they enter.

This is our task in the new season. Everything we have from God (faith, Baptism, the Holy Qurbono, the prayer our parents taught us) came to us as a gift. Let us give it away as a gift: in a visit, a lesson, a kind word, a hand held out. The Spirit is not given to be kept but to be shared. Amen.
kids: Children, yesterday was Pentecost, the birthday of the Church, when the Holy Spirit came like fire. Today Jesus sends his friends out. He told them: you received without payment; give without payment. That means: God gave you many good things for nothing, your family, your food, your faith. Now you can give for nothing too! Can you help someone today without asking for anything back?

homily: Dear friends, the Letter to the Hebrews tells us how far God came to find us. Since the children share flesh and blood, he himself likewise shared the same things, so that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death (Hebrews 2:14). The Son did not save us from a distance. He took our body, so that he could meet death from the inside and defeat it.

Therefore he had to become like his brothers and sisters in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest (Hebrews 2:17). Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested (Hebrews 2:18). When we pray in temptation, we speak to one who has been there.

In the Gospel Jesus gives us a homely picture of this mercy. A woman loses one of her ten silver coins. She lights a lamp, sweeps the house, and searches carefully until she finds it (Luke 15:8). Then she calls her friends and neighbours to rejoice. Just so, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents (Luke 15:10).

St Gregory the Great saw in the lamp the divinity of Christ shining in our flesh. The Spirit now puts that lamp in our hands. Let us search for those who are lost: pray for them, make the first move, keep looking. And if we ourselves are the lost coin, let us come to Confession and let heaven rejoice. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever lost something precious, a toy or a pencil box, and looked everywhere for it? Jesus told a story about a woman who lost one coin. She lit a lamp, swept the whole house, and looked under everything until she found it. Then she was so happy that she called all her friends! Jesus says God looks for us like that when we go away from him, and heaven is full of joy when we come back.

homily: Dear friends, today our Church remembers Mar Yaqob Shleeha offering the Holy Qurbono for the first time. Our tradition honours St James of Jerusalem, the Lord's brother, the first bishop of that city, to whom the Anaphora of St James is ascribed, the source of the Qurbono we celebrate. After Pentecost the first Christians devoted themselves to the breaking of bread and the prayers (Acts 2:42).

St Paul tells us how the Qurbono came to us: For I received from the Lord what I also handed on to you (1 Corinthians 11:23). On the night when he was betrayed, the Lord took bread and said, This is my body that is for you. Do this in remembrance of me (1 Corinthians 11:24). From the upper room, through St James and the apostles, through the centuries, this gift has been handed on to our own altar.

In the Gospel we hear the longing of Jesus: I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer (Luke 22:15). He gives the bread and says, This is my body, which is given for you; he gives the cup, the new covenant in my blood (Luke 22:19–20). What we receive is not a symbol only. It is truly his Body and his Blood, his one sacrifice made present.

For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes (1 Corinthians 11:26). Let us thank God today for every priest who has offered the Qurbono for us. Let us come early, prepare our hearts, and receive the Lord as one who longs to feed us. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know what the Holy Qurbono is? It is the greatest gift Jesus gave us. At the Last Supper he said: This is my body, this is my blood, do this in memory of me. Today we remember St James, who offered the Qurbono in Jerusalem long, long ago. He prayed so much that his knees became hard! Next time you go to the Qurbono, remember: Jesus really comes to us, and he is very happy to see you.

homily: Dear friends, today our Church honours the Four Evangelists, Matthew, Mark, Luke and John. Matthew the tax collector, Mark who wrote down Peter's preaching, Luke the physician and companion of Paul, John the beloved disciple. Four voices, one Lord. St Irenaeus said that the Gospel is fourfold, held together by one Spirit.

St Paul tells us why they matter: how are they to believe in one of whom they have never heard? And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him? (Romans 10:14). So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ (Romans 10:17). Someone was sent, someone wrote, someone read it to us. How beautiful are the feet of those who bring good news! (Romans 10:15).

In the Gospel the risen Lord meets the eleven on the mountain. They worshiped him; but some doubted (Matthew 28:17). Even so, he sends them: Go therefore and make disciples of all nations, and he promises: I am with you always, to the end of the age (Matthew 28:19–20). He is with us in the Qurbono and in the word. That is why we stand when the Evangelion is proclaimed.

Let us honour the evangelists by reading what they wrote. Take one Gospel and read a chapter a day. Read it with your family. Then share it: faith comes from what is heard, and someone near you is waiting to hear. Amen.
kids: Children, who wrote the stories of Jesus that we hear in church? Four friends of Jesus: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John! We call them the evangelists, which means people who bring good news. In pictures, Matthew has a man, Mark a lion, Luke an ox and John an eagle. At the end of Matthew's book, Jesus says: I am with you always. Whenever you hear the Gospel, Jesus is talking to you! Can you ask your parents to read you one story from a Gospel tonight?

homily: Dear friends, today is Golden Friday, the first Friday after Pentecost. Our Church remembers the first miracle the apostles worked in the name of Jesus after receiving the Spirit. Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, at three o'clock in the afternoon (Acts 3:1), and at the Beautiful Gate lay a man lame from birth, asking for alms.

Peter looked intently at him and said, Look at us. The man expected a coin. But Peter said, I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, stand up and walk (Acts 3:6). He took him by the right hand and raised him up, and the man entered the temple, walking and leaping and praising God (Acts 3:8). The one who had sat outside the gate all his life now went in. That is the gold of the Church: the name of Jesus.

St Paul tells us that this gold is love. If I have all faith, so as to remove mountains, but do not have love, I am nothing (1 Corinthians 13:2). Love is patient; love is kind (1 Corinthians 13:4). Peter's miracle was love that stopped, looked, touched and lifted. Without love, even our good works are only a noisy gong.

In the Gospel Jesus warns that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God; but for God all things are possible (Matthew 19:24, 26). Peter left everything, and found himself richer than anyone. St Helena, whom we also remember today, spent the riches of an empire on churches and on the poor. So let us ask: what is my gold, and whose hands is it in? Let us give what we have, in the name of Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, today is called Golden Friday! Do you know why? After the Holy Spirit came, Peter and John met a man who could not walk. He asked them for money. Peter said, I have no silver or gold, but in the name of Jesus, stand up and walk! And the man jumped up and danced into the temple, praising God! Peter had no gold, but he had Jesus, and that is better than all the gold in the world. What can you give someone today, even if you have no money? A smile, a helping hand, a prayer!

intro: Peter and John were going up to the Temple at the hour of prayer. The first miracle after Pentecost happened on the way to ordinary, daily prayer.

sub: Three o'clock in the afternoon.
Daniel prayed three times a day.
The Spirit-filled Church keeps the hours.
points.apply: Choose fixed times of prayer each day, morning and evening, and keep them.

sub: Peter and John together.
Day by day in the Temple.
Prayer that is shared.
points.apply: Pray together as a family at least once each day.

points.h: He entered the Temple with them
sub: The man who sat outside the gate.
Now he goes in.
The Church brings people inside.
points.apply: Invite someone who has stopped coming to the Holy Qurbono to come with you.

concl: The Spirit-filled apostles did not stop praying at fixed hours; their miracle happened on the way to prayer.
A praying Church brings those outside the gate into the house of God.
opts.resolve: This week I will keep fixed times of prayer, pray with my family, and invite one person to come with me to the Holy Qurbono.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Golden Friday, when our Church remembers the first miracle of the apostles after Pentecost. Saint Luke begins the story very simply: one day Peter and John were going up to the temple at the hour of prayer, at three o'clock in the afternoon (Acts 3:1). The Spirit had come down with wind and fire, but the apostles did not abandon the ordinary rhythm of prayer. They still went up at the fixed hour.

Prayer at fixed hours is very old. The prophet Daniel, even under threat of death, got down on his knees three times a day to pray to his God and praise him (Daniel 6:10). Our own Syriac tradition has kept the hours of prayer, morning and evening and through the day. The Holy Spirit does not make fixed prayer unnecessary. He fills it with life.

Notice also that Peter and John went together. Saint Luke says of the first Christians: day by day, as they spent much time together in the temple, they broke bread at home (Acts 2:46). The Psalm sings: I was glad when they said to me, let us go to the house of the Lord! (Psalm 122:1). Prayer is personal, but it is never private in the sense of being alone. We pray as a Church, and families pray together.

And see what happened at the gate. A man lame from birth had been carried there every day. He sat outside, at the door of the house of God, but he never went in. After Peter raised him up, he entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God (Acts 3:8). The Psalm says: I would rather be a doorkeeper in the house of my God than live in the tents of wickedness (Psalm 84:10). The first fruit of the Spirit-filled Church was to bring someone from outside the gate to the inside.

So on this Golden Friday let us keep fixed times of prayer, morning and evening. Let us pray together as families. And let us think of someone who sits outside the gate, who once came to the Holy Qurbono and no longer does, and invite them to come in with us. That is the gold the Church has to give. Amen.

opts.a: What then will we have? The hundredfold
intro: After the rich young man went away, Peter asked: we have left everything; what then will we have? Jesus promises a hundredfold and eternal life. Golden Friday shows the true riches of the disciple.

sub: The rich young man's sorrow.
Peter's question.
Following Christ costs something.
points.apply: Give up one thing this week that keeps you from following Christ fully.

sub: Isaac sowed and reaped a hundredfold.
A new family in the Church.
Eternal life.
points.apply: Thank God for the brothers and sisters he has given you in the Church.

sub: God raises up the poor.
The world's order reversed.
Peter, a poor fisherman, becomes rich in Christ.
points.apply: Serve someone this week whom others overlook.

concl: Nothing given up for Christ is lost; he repays it a hundredfold.
The true riches of the disciple are the name of Jesus, the family of the Church and eternal life.
opts.resolve: This week I will give up one thing for Christ, thank him for my Church family, and serve someone who is overlooked.
homily: Dear friends, today's Gospel comes right after a sad scene. A rich young man had asked Jesus what he must do to have eternal life, and when Jesus told him to sell his possessions and follow him, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions. Then Jesus said: it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for someone who is rich to enter the kingdom of God (Matthew 19:24).

Peter, always quick to speak, asks the question that is in all our hearts: look, we have left everything and followed you. What then will we have? (Matthew 19:27). It is an honest question. Abraham too had left his country and his father's house at God's word (Genesis 12:1). Following Christ costs something. Every disciple has left something behind.

Jesus does not scold Peter. He makes a promise: everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or children or fields, for my name's sake, will receive a hundredfold, and will inherit eternal life (Matthew 19:29). In Genesis we read that Isaac sowed seed in that land, and in the same year reaped a hundredfold (Genesis 26:12). What is the hundredfold? It is the new family Jesus gives us in the Church: brothers and sisters, fathers and mothers in faith, a home in every parish. And beyond all this, eternal life.

Then Jesus adds: many who are first will be last, and the last will be first (Matthew 19:30). Hannah sang the same truth: he raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap (1 Samuel 2:8). On Golden Friday we remember that a poor fisherman, who had no silver or gold, raised a lame man in the name of Jesus. Peter, who had left his nets, had become richer than any king.

So let us ask: what is holding me back from following Christ fully? Let us give one thing up this week for his sake. Let us thank God for the family he has given us in the Church. And let us serve someone whom others overlook, because in God's kingdom the last will be first. Amen.

Dear friends, St Paul tells the Corinthians that he does not need letters of recommendation. You yourselves are our letter, written on our hearts, to be known and read by all (2 Corinthians 3:2). They are a letter of Christ, written not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets of human hearts (2 Corinthians 3:3). This is what Pentecost does: the Spirit writes God's law on our hearts.

For the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). A command written outside us tells us what to do; the Spirit within gives us the strength to do it. As St Augustine said (in substance), we can now pray: Lord, give what you command. The glory that shone on Moses' face is meant to shine quietly in our ordinary lives.

In the Gospel, ten bridesmaids wait for the bridegroom. All of them fall asleep; the difference is the oil. The foolish ask to borrow at the last moment, but the oil of a lifetime cannot be borrowed. Keep awake therefore, for you know neither the day nor the hour (Matthew 25:13). Our oil is prayer and works of mercy, kept up day after day.

Today we remember St Rita, whose lamp burned through a long night: a hard marriage, the murder of her husband, the loss of her sons, and through it all patience, prayer and forgiveness. Let us ask her prayers for families in difficulty and for causes that seem impossible, and let us keep our lamps filled, so that our lives are letters in which others can read Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul says something surprising: you are a letter! Not a letter written with a pen, but a letter written by the Holy Spirit on your heart. When people see how you behave, kind or unkind, patient or angry, they are reading that letter. Today we remember St Rita, who stayed gentle and kept praying even when her life was very hard. Let's be letters that tell everyone how good Jesus is!

homily: Dear friends, a week ago the Holy Spirit came at Pentecost. Today St Paul tells us what the Spirit is doing: you are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God (Ephesians 2:19). Each one of us has been brought in from outside and given a place at the table.

Paul says we are built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone (Ephesians 2:20). And the building is still going up: in him the whole structure is joined together and grows into a holy temple in the Lord (Ephesians 2:21). The Spirit is the builder, and he fits us together, stone beside stone. Sometimes that fitting is painful, when we must forgive or work patiently with others. But that is how a house is made.

The Gospel shows a sad picture. Many, even of the authorities, believed in Jesus, but because of the Pharisees they did not confess it, for fear that they would be put out of the synagogue (John 12:42). John explains why: for they loved human glory more than the glory that comes from God (John 12:43). They believed, but they hid it. That temptation is not far from us.

So let us ask two things today. First, let the Holy Spirit fit us together in love, in our homes and in our parish. Second, let us not be ashamed of the house we belong to. A small sign of the Cross, a kind word for the Church, a quiet witness at work: these are the stones of a living temple. Amen.
kids: Children, have you ever watched people building a house? First they lay a strong stone at the corner, and then they put the other stones next to it, one by one. St Paul says the Church is God's house, and Jesus is the corner stone. Each of you is a stone too! The Holy Spirit puts us next to each other, so we must be kind and not push each other away. And when your friends ask about Jesus, do not be shy. Be proud to belong to God's house.

homily: Dear friends, today the Panchangam remembers St Sophia. Her name means wisdom, and St Paul shows us what Christian wisdom looks like: so we do not lose heart. Even though our outer nature is wasting away, our inner nature is being renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16).

Paul calls his many sufferings a slight momentary affliction, because they are preparing us for an eternal weight of glory beyond all measure (2 Corinthians 4:17). He has put them on a scale next to heaven. And he tells us where to look: what can be seen is temporary, but what cannot be seen is eternal (2 Corinthians 4:18).

In the Gospel Jesus tells of a nobleman who gave his servants a pound each and said: do business with these until I come back (Luke 19:13). Two used it well and were praised: because you have been trustworthy in a very small thing, take charge of ten cities (Luke 19:17). One hid it in a cloth because he was afraid. The Lord has given each of us faith, gifts and time. This is the time between his Ascension and his return.

Let us not lose heart when the body grows weak, and let us not bury what we have received. A visit to a sick person, a song in the choir, an hour with a child learning the catechism: these are the pounds we trade for the kingdom. With St Sophia, let us choose the wisdom that looks at what cannot be seen. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told a story about a king who gave his helpers some money and said: use it well until I come back. Two helpers worked hard and made more. One was scared and hid the money in a cloth. God has given each of you something special: maybe you sing well, or draw, or you are good at making friends. Do not hide it! Use it to make someone happy and to make God happy too.

homily: Dear friends, in the Gospel today many disciples have left Jesus because his teaching about the bread of life seemed too hard. Jesus does not run after them and change his words. He turns to the Twelve and asks: do you also wish to go away? (John 6:67).

Peter answers: Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life. We have come to believe and know that you are the Holy One of God (John 6:68–69). Peter does not understand everything. But he knows that no other road leads to life. That is our faith when we come to the Holy Qurbono.

St Paul thanks God that the Thessalonians received the gospel not as a human word but as what it really is, God's word, which is also at work in you believers (1 Thessalonians 2:13). The word of God works. It changed the Thessalonians, and it changed a young man in Rome named Philip Neri, whom we remember today. On the eve of Pentecost 1544, his life tells us, the fire of the Spirit filled his heart. He became a priest who heard confessions for hours, who loved the Eucharist, and who made a whole city smile.

So when following Jesus is hard, let us not walk away. Let us say with Peter: to whom can we go? And let us ask St Philip Neri to pray for us, that our faith may be joyful, humble and full of the Holy Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, once Jesus said something that was hard to understand, and many people went away. Jesus asked his friends: are you going too? Peter said: no, Lord, we will stay with you! Today we also remember St Philip Neri. He was a priest who loved Jesus so much that he was always happy. He laughed and played with children and told them: be good, if you can! When you love Jesus, you can be joyful too.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul writes: so if you have been raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, seated at the right hand of God (Colossians 3:1). We saw the Lord ascend three weeks ago. Now we must live with our hearts turned towards him.

Paul tells us a secret about ourselves: for you have died, and your life is hidden with Christ in God (Colossians 3:3). In Baptism our true life was hidden in God, like a seed under the ground. One day, when Christ who is your life is revealed, then you also will be revealed with him in glory (Colossians 3:4).

In the Gospel a great crowd is pressing round Jesus. But one woman, sick for twelve years, came up behind him and touched the fringe of his clothes, and immediately her hemorrhage stopped (Luke 8:44). Jesus knew: someone touched me; for I noticed that power had gone out from me (Luke 8:46). Many were near him; only she touched him with faith. And he called her: daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace (Luke 8:48).

At every Holy Qurbono we are in a crowd near Jesus. Let us not only press. Let us reach out with faith, bring our hidden wounds, and receive him who is our life. Then we too will hear his word of peace. Amen.
kids: Children, imagine a huge crowd pushing around Jesus. A lady who was very sick for a long time crept up behind him and touched just the edge of his clothes, and she was healed! Jesus stopped and said: who touched me? He wanted to meet her and make her happy. Jesus is never too busy for you. When you pray, it is like touching his cloak. He always notices you.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul could not stop worrying about the new Christians in Thessalonica. So he sent Timothy, our brother and co-worker for God in proclaiming the gospel of Christ, to strengthen and encourage you for the sake of your faith, so that no one would be shaken by these persecutions (1 Thessalonians 3:2–3).

Paul is afraid of one thing: that somehow the tempter had tempted you and that our labor had been in vain (1 Thessalonians 3:5). The tempter often works through tiredness and discouragement. And the Church answers by sending people to strengthen one another. Each of us can be a Timothy for someone this week.

In the Gospel Jesus watches people giving money in the temple. Many rich people put in large sums. A poor widow came and put in two small copper coins (Mark 12:41–42). And Jesus says: for all of them have contributed out of their abundance; but she out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on (Mark 12:44). God sees what no one else sees.

Today is Friday, the day of the Cross. On the Cross Jesus gave not two coins but his whole life. When we bring our offering to the Holy Qurbono, let us bring ourselves with it. And let us go out to encourage someone who is shaken. Amen.
kids: Children, one day Jesus sat in the temple and watched people putting money in the offering box. Rich people put in lots of money, clink, clink, clink! Then a poor lady put in just two tiny coins. Jesus said: she gave the most of all! Why? Because she gave everything she had. God does not count how big our gift is. He looks at how much love is in it. What can you give to God with all your love?

homily: Dear friends, tomorrow is Vocations Day, and St Paul speaks to us about shepherds. He left Titus in Crete so that you should put in order what remained to be done, and should appoint elders in every town (Titus 1:5). The Church has always needed shepherds, and she still does.

Paul says: for a bishop, as God's steward, must be blameless (Titus 1:7). He must be hospitable, a lover of goodness, prudent, upright, devout, and self-controlled (Titus 1:8). He must hold fast to the trustworthy word. These virtues are also for each of us, and they are learned first at home. Good priests come from homes where prayer is kept and the Qurbono is loved.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the crowds the price of following him: whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple (Luke 14:27). He does not ask us to stop loving our families. He asks to be loved first, above everything, even above our own life.

Today we remember St Theodosia. The Panchangam does not tell us which saint of that name is meant, but the martyrs who bore that name loved Christ more than their own lives. Let us pray tomorrow for vocations, let us thank God for our priests, and let us carry our own cross behind Jesus with love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said that if we want to be his friends and followers, we must carry our cross. What does that mean? It means doing the right thing even when it is hard: being kind to someone who is not kind to you, helping at home when you would rather play, telling the truth when you are scared. Tomorrow is Vocations Day. Maybe Jesus is calling one of you to be a priest or a sister one day! Let us pray for that.

homily: Dear friends, St Paul gives thanks for the Christians of Thessalonica, because your faith is growing abundantly, and the love of every one of you for one another is increasing (2 Thessalonians 1:3). They are suffering persecution, and still they are growing. Faith and love grow together.

In the Gospel Jesus looks up to heaven on the night before he dies and prays: Father, the hour has come; glorify your Son so that the Son may glorify you (John 17:1). The hour of the Cross is the hour of glory, because there the love of God is shown to all.

Then Jesus tells us what eternal life is: and this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent (John 17:3). Eternal life begins now. It is not only knowing about God, but knowing him, as a child knows a father. We come to know him in prayer, in the Gospel and above all in the Holy Qurbono.

Today the month of May ends, the month of the Mother of God, and the Latin Church keeps the feast of the Visitation. No one knew Jesus better than his holy Mother. Let us ask her to help us know her Son, to grow in faith and in love, and to carry him to others as she carried him to Elizabeth. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know the difference between knowing about someone and knowing them? You may know about the Prime Minister, but you know your mother! Jesus said that eternal life is knowing God, really knowing him like a friend and a Father. How do we get to know God? By talking to him every day, by listening to his stories in the Bible, and by meeting Jesus in the Holy Qurbono. Today is the last day of Mary's month. Ask Mother Mary to help you know Jesus better.

intro: Theme: “Your pain will turn into joy.”

Before his Passion Jesus prepared his disciples for sorrow, and promised a joy no one could take away. In the Easter season the Church hears these words as fulfilled, and learns that the Spirit of truth leads us into this joy.

sub: Jesus compares the disciples' grief to a mother in labour: pain that gives way to new life.
The Psalmist knew: weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
Easter joy does not deny suffering; it passes through it.
q: Weeping may linger for the night, but joy comes with the morning.
So you have pain now; but I will see you again, and your hearts will rejoice, and no one will take your joy from you.
points.apply: Offer one present sorrow to the Lord, trusting it will become joy.

sub: God's counsel is wonderful and his wisdom excellent.
Jesus promises the Spirit of truth who will guide us into all truth.
The Spirit speaks through Scripture and the teaching of the Church, never against them.
q: This also comes from the LORD of hosts; he is wonderful in counsel, and excellent in wisdom.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all the truth.
points.apply: Before every decision this week, pray: “Come, Holy Spirit, guide me.”

sub: At the feast of Weeks all rejoiced together: children, servants, strangers, orphans and widows.
The first disciples, though persecuted, were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit.
Christian joy is never selfish; it includes the poor and the lonely.
q: Rejoice before the LORD your God—you and your sons and your daughters, your male and female slaves, the Levites resident in your towns, as well as the strangers, the orphans, and the widows who are among you.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
points.apply: Invite someone lonely to share a family meal or celebration.

concl: The Risen Lord gives a joy that the world cannot give or take away.
Let us ask in his name, let the Spirit guide us, and share our joy with all.
2027-05-02.resolve: Begin preparing for Pentecost: pray each day “Come, Holy Spirit.”

intro: Theme: “He was carried up into heaven, blessing them.”
Forty days after his Resurrection the Lord ascends. It is not a farewell of absence but of glory: our human nature, in Christ, enters heaven, and the Church is sent to the ends of the earth.

sub: Elijah was taken up in a whirlwind; Elisha received his spirit.
Jesus lifts up his hands and blesses the disciples; while blessing them he is carried up.
His last gesture on earth is blessing: his hands remain raised over the Church.
q: As they continued walking and talking, a chariot of fire and horses of fire separated the two of them, and Elijah ascended in a whirlwind into heaven.
Then he led them out as far as Bethany, and, lifting up his hands, he blessed them. While he was blessing them, he withdrew from them and was carried up into heaven.
points.apply: Receive the final blessing at every Qurbono as Christ's own blessing.

points.h: Seated at the right hand of the Father
sub: The Psalm foretold: “Sit at my right hand.”
Christ, true God and true man, takes our humanity into the glory of the Father.
There he intercedes for us as our High Priest; where the Head has gone, the members hope to follow (CCC 661–667).
q: The LORD says to my lord, “Sit at my right hand until I make your enemies your footstool.”
So then the Lord Jesus, after he had spoken to them, was taken up into heaven and sat down at the right hand of God.
points.apply: Lift your heart to heaven each day: “Lord, draw me to where you are.”

points.h: Why stand looking up? Be witnesses
sub: The prophets saw that the spirit of Elijah rested on Elisha.
The angels ask: “Why do you stand looking up toward heaven?” He will come again.
Meanwhile, with the power of the Spirit, we are witnesses to the ends of the earth.
q: When the company of prophets who were at Jericho saw him at a distance, they declared, “The spirit of Elijah rests on Elisha.”
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
points.apply: Begin the novena to the Holy Spirit with Mary, from tomorrow until Pentecost.

concl: The Ascension is the feast of our hope: our humanity is in heaven with Christ.
Let us return like the apostles “with great joy”, praying with Mary for the Spirit.
2027-05-06.resolve: Pray the novena to the Holy Spirit from the Ascension to Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “Waiting for the Spirit with Mary.”

Between the Ascension and Pentecost the Church waits in the upper room. Jesus has said it is better for us that he goes, for then the Advocate will come. His high-priestly prayer asks that we may all be one.

sub: The apostles, with Mary and the women, devote themselves to prayer.
Waiting is not idleness; it is opening the heart to God's gift.
God's spirit already fills all things; we pray that he fill us anew.
q: For your immortal spirit is in all things.
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers.
points.apply: Pray the Rosary each day this week for a new Pentecost in your family.

points.h: Better for you that I go
sub: Jesus' bodily presence was in one place; the Spirit makes him present everywhere.
The Spirit convicts the world of sin, not to condemn but to heal.
Isaiah: God sweeps away our sins like mist and calls us back.
q: I have swept away your transgressions like a cloud, and your sins like mist; return to me, for I have redeemed you.
It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
points.apply: Ask the Holy Spirit to show you one sin to be healed, and confess it.

points.h: That they may all be one
sub: God promised: “I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.”
Jesus prays that his disciples be one as he and the Father are one.
Unity in families, parishes and among Christians is the Spirit's work and our task.
q: I will take you as my people, and I will be your God.
That they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Heal one division before Pentecost: call, visit or forgive.

concl: The upper room teaches us to wait, pray and seek unity.
Let us prepare with Mary for the coming of the Spirit next Sunday.
2027-05-09.resolve: Pray daily until Pentecost: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill the hearts of your faithful.”

intro: Theme: “All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit.”

Fifty days after Easter the promise of the Father is fulfilled. Wind and fire fill the upper room; frightened disciples become bold witnesses; people of many languages hear the wonders of God. The Church is born into mission.

points.h: A new heart and a new spirit
sub: Ezekiel promised a heart of flesh for a heart of stone, and God's own Spirit within.
At Pentecost the promise is fulfilled: wind fills the house, tongues of fire rest on each.
The same Spirit came upon us in Baptism and Chrismation with holy Myron.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. I will put my spirit within you.

Divided tongues, as of fire, appeared among them, and a tongue rested on each of them. All of them were filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak in other languages, as the Spirit gave them ability.
points.apply: Thank God today for your Chrismation, and ask the Spirit to rekindle its grace.

points.h: One Spirit for all God's people
sub: Moses longed that all the Lord's people be prophets.
At Pentecost the Spirit is given not to a few but to all, young and old, men and women.
Many languages hear one Gospel: Babel's division is healed in the Church.
q: Would that all the LORD's people were prophets, and that the LORD would put his spirit on them!
In our own languages we hear them speaking about God's deeds of power.
points.apply: Use the gift the Spirit gave you (music, teaching, caring) in the service of your parish.

points.h: The Advocate who teaches and transforms
sub: When the Spirit came upon Saul, he was “turned into a different person”.
Jesus promised the Advocate who teaches everything and reminds us of his words.
The Spirit does not replace Christ; he makes Christ alive in us.
q: Then the spirit of the LORD will possess you … and be turned into a different person.
But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything, and remind you of all that I have said to you.
points.apply: Read one chapter of the Acts of the Apostles each day this week.

concl: Pentecost is the birthday of the Church and the fulfilment of Easter.
Let us live by the Spirit, speak the language of love, and bear witness to Christ everywhere.
2027-05-16.resolve: Pray each morning this week: “Come, Holy Spirit, fill my heart and kindle in me the fire of your love.”

intro: Theme: “The Spirit bears fruit in good soil.”
After Pentecost the Church asks what difference the Spirit makes. The answer is fruit: a heart that receives the Word, a life that shows love and joy, and a people fed by the bread that endures.

sub: The seed is the word of God; the soil is the human heart.
Good soil hears the word, holds it fast and bears fruit with patience.
Jeremiah: those who seek God with all their heart will find him.
q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart.
But as for that in the good soil, these are the ones who, when they hear the word, hold it fast in an honest and good heart, and bear fruit with patient endurance.
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again each evening this week and keep one word in your heart.

sub: Micah was filled with the spirit of the Lord to speak truth with courage.
St Paul names the fruit: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control.
If we live by the Spirit, let us also be guided by the Spirit.
q: But as for me, I am filled with power, with the spirit of the LORD, and with justice and might.
By contrast, the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, generosity, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.
points.apply: Choose one fruit of the Spirit and practise it deliberately each day this week.

points.h: Bread that endures and a plan for each life
sub: Jesus urges us to work for the food that endures for eternal life.
God has plans for our welfare, a future with hope: every life has a vocation.
The Spirit leads young people to discover their call: priesthood, religious life, marriage.
q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures for eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you.
points.apply: Pray for vocations, and encourage a young person to listen to God's call.

concl: The Spirit sows, nourishes and makes us fruitful.
Let us be good soil, bear his fruit, and feed on the bread that endures.
2027-05-23.resolve: Each night this week, examine: which fruit of the Spirit did I show today?

intro: Theme: “Called after a night of prayer.”

Jesus spends the night in prayer, chooses the Twelve, and proclaims the Beatitudes. The Spirit poured out at Pentecost makes this way of life possible for all of us: chosen, blessed, and called to holiness.

sub: Jesus spends the whole night in prayer before choosing the apostles.
He calls each by name and names them apostles, “sent ones”.
As God was with David, so he is with those he calls.
q: And David became greater and greater, for the LORD, the God of hosts, was with him.
Now during those days he went out to the mountain to pray; and he spent the night in prayer to God. And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles.
points.apply: Before an important decision this week, spend extra time in prayer.

sub: Jesus calls the poor, the hungry and those who weep “blessed”.
Their hope is in the kingdom that God promised, a kingdom that will never be destroyed.
The Beatitudes turn the world's values upside down.
q: For he is the living God, enduring forever. His kingdom shall never be destroyed, and his dominion has no end.
Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God. Blessed are you who are hungry now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.
points.apply: Thank God for one blessing hidden in a present difficulty.

points.h: Be holy: the cross and the cup of water
sub: God's command to Israel: “You shall be holy, for I am holy.”
Holiness means taking up the cross and following Jesus.
It also means small kindnesses: even a cup of cold water given in his name.
q: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
Whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones in the name of a disciple—truly I tell you, none of these will lose their reward.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of kindness each day this week.

concl: Prayer, poverty of spirit and humble love are the marks of those whom Christ calls.
Let the Spirit of Pentecost make us holy in great crosses and small kindnesses.
2027-05-30.resolve: Read the Beatitudes (Luke 6:20–26) each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “Is not this the carpenter’s son?”
On May Day, with Mar Yauseph, Patron of Workers, and Jeremiah the Prophet: the hidden workshop, the dignity of labour, and the clay in the potter's hand.

sub: The Son of God in a workshop.
Holiness done with the hands.
A title of honour, not of shame.
q: The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.
Whatever your task, put yourselves into it, as done for the Lord and not for your masters,
points.apply: Choose one ordinary task today and do it as carefully as if Jesus were working beside you.

points.h: Work quietly and earn your living
sub: Paul the tentmaker.
Idleness, the enemy of the soul.
Work that has something to share.
q: Go to the ant, you lazybones; consider its ways, and be wise.
Thieves must give up stealing; rather let them labor and work honestly with their own hands, so as to have something to share with the needy.
points.apply: Set aside a small part of this month's earnings or pocket money for someone in need.

sub: Known before the womb.
Rejected in his own town.
Clay on the wheel.
q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.
Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in the prophet’s hometown.
points.apply: Where you are not appreciated at home or at work, keep doing what is right, and let God shape you there.

concl: Mar Yauseph shows that the hidden work of the hands can serve the Son of God.
Jeremiah reminds us that God shapes his servants like clay, even through rejection.
2027-05-01.resolve: Offer each day's work to God, work honestly, share with the needy, and pray for all workers.

intro: Theme: “See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!”
On Monday of the fifth week after Qyomtho, three days before Suloko: God's today, the riches of the poor apostle, and the light of the world.

points.h: Now is the day of salvation
sub: Grace not received in vain.
Not yesterday, not someday.
Preparing now for the Ascension and the Spirit.
q: In a time of favor I have answered you, on a day of salvation I have helped you;
Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.
points.apply: Write down one thing you have postponed for God and set a day this week to do it.

points.h: Having nothing, and yet possessing everything
sub: The hardships of an apostle.
The weapons of righteousness.
Joy that survives sorrow.
q: The Lord is my chosen portion and my cup; you hold my lot.
I can do all things through him who strengthens me.
points.apply: In one difficulty you face this week, thank God aloud for something he has given you in it.

sub: Spoken in the temple treasury.
The Father bears witness.
Walking in the light.
q: The Lord is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear?
but if we walk in the light as he himself is in the light, we have fellowship with one another, and the blood of Jesus his Son cleanses us from all sin.
points.apply: Pray the morning prayer of the Shehimo, or a short morning prayer, each day this week, greeting Christ as your light.

concl: God's time is today; grace postponed is grace wasted.
The one who has Christ has everything and walks in his light.
2027-05-03.resolve: Do today the good you have postponed, rejoice in trouble, and walk in the light of Christ as you prepare for Suloko.

intro: Theme: “Not only the gospel of God but also our own selves.”
On Tuesday of the fifth week after Qyomtho: the pure motive of the preacher, the gentleness of a nurse and the firmness of a father, and the word that conquers death.

points.h: To please God who tests our hearts
sub: Courage in our God.
No flattery, no greed.
The heart behind the message.
q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart.
Am I now seeking human approval, or God’s approval? Or am I trying to please people? If I were still pleasing people, I would not be a servant of Christ.
points.apply: Before you speak about God or give advice this week, ask silently: am I seeking to please God or to be admired?

points.h: Gentle like a nurse, firm like a father
sub: Tenderness in ministry.
Urging and encouraging.
Sharing our own selves.
q: He will feed his flock like a shepherd; he will gather the lambs in his arms, and carry them in his bosom, and gently lead the mother sheep.
No one has greater love than this, to lay down one’s life for one’s friends.
points.apply: Give one person an hour of undivided attention this week, without looking at your phone.

points.h: Whoever keeps my word will never see death
sub: Insult answered with truth.
The promise of the Risen One.
Keeping his word in small things.
q: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
points.apply: Choose one word of Jesus and practise it deliberately for one whole day.

concl: The Gospel passes from life to life when its messengers give themselves.
Christ, risen from death, gives life to all who keep his word.
2027-05-04.resolve: Seek to please God, share yourself generously, answer insults with truth, and keep one word of Jesus each day.

intro: Theme: “But the Lord is faithful; he will strengthen you and guard you from the evil one.”
On the eve of Suloko: prayer for the word that runs, the faithfulness of God, and the healthy eye that fills the body with light.

sub: The apostle leans on the Church's prayer.
The word that runs.
Mission begins on our knees.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
At the same time pray for us as well that God will open to us a door for the word, that we may declare the mystery of Christ,
points.apply: Pray each day this week by name for your bishop, your parish priest and one missionary.

sub: Not all have faith; God never fails.
Guarded from the evil one.
Hearts directed to love and steadfastness.
q: The steadfast love of the Lord never ceases, his mercies never come to an end; they are new every morning; great is your faithfulness.
God is faithful, and he will not let you be tested beyond your strength, but with the testing he will also provide the way out so that you may be able to endure it.
points.apply: Learn 2 Thessalonians 3:5 by heart and pray it over your family this week.

points.h: Your eye is the lamp of your body
sub: The lamp on the stand.
A healthy eye.
Looking up to the ascending Lord.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: Make a short examination of your eyes each night this week, and give up one thing that darkens you.

concl: The word of the Lord runs when the Church prays, and the faithful Lord guards those who carry it.
A healthy eye makes the whole life a lamp for others.
2027-05-05.resolve: Pray for those who preach, trust the faithful Lord, guard your eyes, and come to Suloko with your heart lifted up.

intro: Theme: “May I never boast of anything except the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ.”
On the Finding of the Cross and First Friday, the day after Suloko: boasting only in the Cross, the treasure hidden in a field, and the pierced Heart of Jesus.

sub: In Paul's own large letters.
The world crucified to me.
A new creation is everything.
q: Make a poisonous serpent, and set it on a pole; and everyone who is bitten shall look at it and live.
For the message about the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God.
points.apply: Make the sign of the Cross openly before meals this week, even in public.

points.h: A treasure hidden in a field
sub: The Cross found in Jerusalem.
Selling all in joy.
The pearl of great value.
q: I will give you the treasures of darkness and riches hidden in secret places,
More than that, I regard everything as loss because of the surpassing value of knowing Christ Jesus my Lord.
points.apply: Name one thing you hold too tightly, and give part of it up this week for Christ.

sub: First Friday.
Blood and water.
The marks of Jesus on our bodies.
q: when they look on the one whom they have pierced, they shall mourn for him, as one mourns for an only child,
Instead, one of the soldiers pierced his side with a spear, and at once blood and water came out.
points.apply: Go to confession before Pentecost, and offer one suffering you carry to the Heart of Jesus.

concl: The ascended Lord is the Crucified; the Cross is the road of his glory and of ours.
Whoever finds the Cross finds the treasure for which everything else may be gladly sold.
2027-05-07.resolve: Sign yourself with the Cross attentively, boast of nothing but Christ crucified, and bring your heart to his pierced Heart in these days of waiting.

intro: Theme: “Who will separate us from the love of Christ?”

On the memory of Mar Yohannan Shleeha and the founding of the Daughters of Mary, in the days of waiting for the Spirit: the beloved disciple, love that nothing can defeat, and the Mother taken into his home.

sub: Resting on the heart of Christ.
“What is that to you? Follow me!”
A witness whose testimony is true.
q: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death,
God is love, and those who abide in love abide in God, and God abides in them.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes in silent prayer this week simply resting in Christ's love, without asking for anything.

sub: Hardship, distress, persecution.
More than conquerors.
Neither death nor life.
q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you;
I give them eternal life, and they will never perish. No one will snatch them out of my hand.
points.apply: Write Romans 8:35 on a card and give it to someone who is suffering.

points.h: He took her into his own home
sub: The Mother given from the Cross.
The Daughters of Mary, 1938.
Waiting for the Spirit with Mary.
q: Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
When Jesus saw his mother and the disciple whom he loved standing beside her, he said to his mother, “Woman, here is your son.”
points.apply: Pray a Marian prayer as a family each evening until Pentecost, and pray for religious vocations.

concl: Mar Yohannan teaches us to rest on the heart of Christ and to love one another.
Like him and like the Daughters of Mary, we take the Mother of the Lord into our home and wait with her for the Spirit.
2027-05-08.resolve: Follow Jesus without comparing, trust that nothing can separate you from his love, and welcome Mary into your home.

intro: Theme: “For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.”
On the memory of Mar Shemun Shleeha the Zealot, in the days of waiting before Pentecost: the apostle with a fiery heart, the tax collector found by grace, and zeal that waits for the Spirit.

points.h: Simon the Zealot: a fire chosen by Christ
sub: The Cananaean, the zealous one.
Waiting in the upper room with Mary.
Zeal turned from anger to love.
q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.
Do not lag in zeal, be ardent in spirit, serve the Lord.
points.apply: Name the thing you are most zealous about and offer it to Jesus in prayer each morning until Pentecost.

points.h: Today salvation has come to this house
sub: A short man in a sycamore tree.
Jesus comes first; goodness follows.
Half to the poor, fourfold to the wronged.
q: I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed
The saying is sure and worthy of full acceptance, that Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners
points.apply: Put right one thing you owe another person, in money, in time or in an apology, before Sunday.

sub: Paul counts the days to Pentecost.
Protecting the young worker.
Zeal that begins on its knees.
q: Wait for the Lord; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the Lord!
All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus, as well as his brothers.
points.apply: Join the novena of prayer for the Holy Spirit with your family each evening until Pentecost.

concl: Jesus chose a zealot and a tax collector and made them brothers; the Spirit purifies our zeal without putting out its fire.
In these ten days the Church waits on its knees, and the Lord stops at every house that longs to see him.
2027-05-10.resolve: Pray for one person you had given up on, put right one wrong, and wait for the Spirit in prayer with Mary.

intro: Theme: “Marked with the seal of the promised Holy Spirit.”
On the memory of Sts Cyril and Methodius, in the days before Pentecost: the night of prayer before the choosing, God's plan to gather all peoples in Christ, and the seal of the Spirit.

points.h: A night of prayer before the choosing
sub: Jesus prays, then calls.
Twelve names, twelve different men.
Mission born from prayer.
q: for the Lord does not see as mortals see; they look on the outward appearance, but the Lord looks on the heart
You did not choose me but I chose you. And I appointed you to go and bear fruit, fruit that will last
points.apply: Before your next important decision, spend one quiet hour in prayer before the icon of Christ.

points.h: All things gathered up in Christ
sub: Two brothers and a new alphabet.
The Gospel at home in every tongue.
One Body of many peoples.
q: I am coming to gather all nations and tongues; and they shall come and shall see my glory
there was a great multitude that no one could count, from every nation, from all tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and before the Lamb
points.apply: Pray this week for one missionary you know, or support a mission in a part of India where the Gospel is new.

sub: The seal of Baptism and Holy Mooron.
The pledge of our inheritance.
Pentecost five days away.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you
But it is God who establishes us with you in Christ and has anointed us, by putting his seal on us and giving us his Spirit in our hearts as a first installment.
points.apply: Each evening until Pentecost, make the sign of the Cross slowly and say, “Come, Holy Spirit, seal me as your own.”

concl: Jesus prayed before he chose; Cyril and Methodius prayed before they wrote; every fruitful mission is born on its knees.
The Spirit who sealed us at Baptism makes the one Gospel speak in every language, until all peoples are gathered in Christ.
2027-05-11.resolve: Pray before your choices, treasure and hand on the prayers of our Church, and ask the Spirit to seal you anew.

intro: Theme: “It is God who is at work in you, enabling you both to will and to work for his good pleasure.”
On the memory of Mar Epiphanios of Cyprus and Mar Yaqob of Nisibis, in the days before Pentecost: grace at work in us, lives that shine, and peace made on the way.

sub: Work out your salvation with fear and trembling.
Grace gives the will and the work.
No contest between God and us.
q: I will put my spirit within you, and make you follow my statutes and be careful to observe my ordinances.
I am confident of this, that the one who began a good work among you will bring it to completion by the day of Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Each night before sleep, thank God for one good thing he did through you that day.

points.h: Shining like stars in the world
sub: Without murmuring and arguing.
Two bishops who guarded the faith of Nicaea.
Honour for Mary, worship for God alone.
q: Those who are wise shall shine like the brightness of the sky, and those who lead many to righteousness, like the stars forever and ever.
You are the light of the world. A city built on a hill cannot be hid.
points.apply: Go three days without complaining, and offer each held-back complaint as a prayer.

points.h: Read the present time; settle it on the way
sub: Watching the western sky in May.
The Spirit is near.
Peace before the gift.
q: Seek the Lord while he may be found, call upon him while he is near;
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
points.apply: Before Pentecost, make one call or visit to someone with whom you need to make peace.

concl: The shepherds of Nisibis and Salamis guarded the faith with zeal; we guard it by shining, not by murmuring.
The Spirit is near like the monsoon; hearts that have made peace on the way will receive him fully.
2027-05-12.resolve: Trust God at work in you, stop murmuring, and make peace on the way before Pentecost.

intro: Theme: “We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
On the memory of Mar Ishaq Malpan of Antioch, three days before Pentecost: the promise sworn by God, hope anchored behind the curtain, and the rivers of living water.

sub: The promise to Abraham.
Patient endurance obtains the promise.
Two unchangeable things.
q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind.
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.”
points.apply: Choose one promise of God from Scripture and pray it every day until Pentecost.

sub: Hope thrown upward, not downward.
Jesus our forerunner and high priest.
The sanctuary curtain at the Holy Qurbono.
q: For God alone my soul waits in silence, for my hope is from him.
and hope does not disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit that has been given to us.
points.apply: When the sanctuary curtain opens at the next Holy Qurbono, offer to Christ the storm you are passing through.

sub: The great day of the feast.
As yet there was no Spirit.
A school of prayer in song.
q: For I will pour water on the thirsty land, and streams on the dry ground; I will pour my spirit upon your descendants, and my blessing on your offspring.
And let everyone who is thirsty come. Let anyone who wishes take the water of life as a gift.
points.apply: Sing or recite one hymn of the Holy Qurbono slowly at home tonight as a prayer for the Spirit.

concl: God's promise cannot fail, and our hope is anchored where Christ has already gone.
The glorified Lord is about to pour out the Spirit; these days are given to make us thirsty.
2027-05-13.resolve: Anchor your hope in Christ, come to him thirsty, and pray in song as Mar Ishaq taught.

intro: Theme: “Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.”
On the feast of Mar Addai Shleeha, two days before Pentecost: the apostle sent after the Ascension, the courage that comes from the Father's care, and the whole Church sharing in mission.

sub: Thomas sends Addai to Edessa.
The Syriac family of faith.
From Jerusalem to the ends of the earth.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation
What I say to you in the dark, tell in the light; and what you hear whispered, proclaim from the housetops.
points.apply: Learn the story of how the faith came to your own family and parish, and tell it to your children.

sub: Those who kill the body.
Five sparrows for two pennies.
Every hair counted.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. I do not give to you as the world gives. Do not let your hearts be troubled, and do not let them be afraid.
points.apply: Write down your greatest fear tonight and place it before an icon of Christ with the words, “Jesus, I trust in you.”

points.h: Sharing the distress of the sent
sub: Paul's secret of contentment.
Strength in him who strengthens.
The Philippians' gift.
q: The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want.
My grace is sufficient for you, for power is made perfect in weakness.
points.apply: Set aside a gift for the missions of your eparchy before Pentecost, and pray for one missionary by name.

concl: Mar Addai went out after the Ascension, and the faith he carried reached the Syriac peoples and, through the same apostolic family, our own Church.
The Father who counts the sparrows counts us; with his Spirit we can speak without fear and give without counting.
2027-05-14.resolve: Speak of Jesus without fear where you are, and share the distress of those who carry him further.

intro: Theme: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
