On the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain and the memory of Mar Pachomios, on the eve of Pentecost: the field that bore the Bread, the blessedness of hearing and keeping, and the cheerful giver.

points.h: The field that bore the Bread
sub: The ears of grain in May.
The Virgin earth and the Bread of life.
Bethlehem, the house of bread.
q: The Lord will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Thank God for your daily bread at each meal today, and pray a Hail Mary for farmers.

sub: The woman in the crowd.
Mary, the first to hear and keep.
Waiting with her for the Spirit.
q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Choose one verse from tomorrow's Pentecost readings and keep it in your heart all week.

sub: Sowing bountifully.
Bread given in a prison at night.
The harvest of righteousness.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
So let us not grow weary in doing what is right, for we will reap at harvest time, if we do not give up.
points.apply: Give food or money to someone in need before tomorrow's Holy Qurbono, gladly and without counting.

concl: The Mother of God is the field that gave the world its Bread; her true blessedness is the word heard and kept.
On the eve of Pentecost we wait with her, sowing bountifully, for the Spirit who brings in God's harvest.
2027-05-15.resolve: Hear God's word and keep it as Mary did, give cheerfully, and wait with her for the Holy Spirit.

intro: Theme: “You received without payment; give without payment.”
On the first Monday of the season of Pentecost: citizens worthy of the gospel, standing side by side, giving as we have received.

sub: Citizens of Christ's city.
Conduct that shows whose we are.
The Spirit in ordinary days.
q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the Lord require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
I therefore, the prisoner in the Lord, beg you to lead a life worthy of the calling to which you have been called
points.apply: Name one place, at work, at home or online, where your conduct does not yet match your Baptism, and change one thing there this week.

sub: One spirit, one mind.
Not intimidated by opponents.
The gift of suffering for Christ.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Now the whole group of those who believed were of one heart and soul
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person in your parish or family with whom you have been at odds.

points.h: Received as gift, given as gift
sub: Sent out with empty belts.
Proclaim, heal, cleanse.
Peace to every house.
q: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” And I said, “Here am I; send me!”
It is more blessed to give than to receive.
points.apply: Offer one skill or one hour each week to someone who cannot pay for it.

concl: The Spirit who came at Pentecost sends the Church out, not with wealth, but with gifts to be given away.
A life worthy of the gospel is a life that gives what it has received, side by side with others and without fear.
2027-05-17.resolve: Live as a citizen of Christ's kingdom, stand with your brothers and sisters, and give without payment what you received without payment.

intro: Theme: “He is able to help those who are being tested.”
On Tuesday after the Sunday of Pentecost: the Son who shared our flesh and blood, the merciful High Priest, and the woman who searches until she finds.

points.h: He shared our flesh and blood
sub: Not rescue from a distance.
Death met from the inside.
Mercy for the children of Abraham.
q: It was no messenger or angel but his presence that saved them; in his love and in his pity he redeemed them
And the Word became flesh and lived among us, and we have seen his glory
points.apply: When you feel your weakness this week, tired, ill or afraid, say quietly: Lord, you know this from the inside.

points.h: A merciful and faithful high priest
sub: Like us in every respect.
Tested by what he suffered.
Able to help us now.
q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the Lord has compassion for those who fear him.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: Go to Confession before the end of this month, and bring the temptation that troubles you most.

sub: One coin out of ten.
The image in the dust.
Joy in the presence of the angels.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
For the Son of Man came to seek out and to save the lost.
points.apply: Pray by name each day this week for one person who has drifted away, and find one simple way to show that you care.

concl: The Son of God came all the way into our flesh, our trials and our death, to find us.
Found by him, we become his lamp, searching for others until heaven rejoices.
2027-05-18.resolve: Bring your trials to the merciful High Priest, and do not rest content while one coin is still lost.

intro: Theme: “Do this in remembrance of me.”
On the memory of Mar Yaqob Shleeha's first offering of the Holy Qurbono: what was received and handed on, the Lord's longing, and the memorial that waits for his coming.

sub: The oldest account of the Supper.
From Jerusalem to our altar.
The Anaphora of St James.
q: This day shall be a day of remembrance for you.
They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers.
points.apply: Learn by heart one response of the Holy Qurbono that you usually only mumble, and say it with meaning next time.

sub: The Lord longs to give himself.
Body given, Blood poured out.
Truly present, not a symbol only.
q: I will lift up the cup of salvation and call on the name of the Lord
I am the living bread that came down from heaven.
points.apply: Make a short visit to the church this week and spend ten minutes before the Lord in the tabernacle.

sub: A living memorial.
One sacrifice made present.
Waiting for his coming.
q: For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations, and in every place incense is offered to my name, and a pure offering
points.apply: After your next Qurbono, do one concrete act of love the same day, so that your life proclaims what you received.

concl: What Mar Yaqob offered in Jerusalem, the Church still offers: the one sacrifice of Christ, received and handed on.
The Lord who eagerly desired to eat the Passover with his disciples still longs to feed us, until he comes.
2027-05-19.resolve: Come to the Holy Qurbono prepared and hungry, thank God for our priests, and let your life proclaim the Lord's death and Resurrection.

intro: Theme: “So faith comes from what is heard.”
On the feast of the Four Evangelists: four voices and one Gospel, the word that is heard and believed, and the Lord who sends and stays with us.

points.h: Faith comes from what is heard
sub: Sent, proclaimed, heard, believed.
Beautiful feet.
The word that stands forever.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
So faith comes from what is heard, and what is heard comes through the word of Christ.
points.apply: Listen to the Evangelion at your next Qurbono as if you were hearing it for the first time, and remember one sentence of it all day.

sub: Matthew, Mark, Luke and John.
Four living creatures around the throne.
Written so that we may believe.
q: As for the appearance of their faces: the four had the face of a human being, the face of a lion on the right side, the face of an ox on the left side, and the face of an eagle
But these are written so that you may come to believe that Jesus is the Messiah, the Son of God, and that through believing you may have life in his name.
points.apply: Choose one Gospel and read it through, one chapter a day, starting today.

sub: Some doubted, and still he sent them.
To all nations.
With us always.
q: yet their voice goes out through all the earth, and their words to the end of the world.
And remember, I am with you always, to the end of the age.
points.apply: Share one Gospel verse this week with someone who is far from faith, simply and without argument.

concl: Through the four evangelists the voice of Christ has gone out to all the earth and reaches us today.
Faith comes from what is heard: what we hear we must also hand on, trusting the Lord who is with us always.
2027-05-20.resolve: Read a Gospel through, listen to the Evangelion as the voice of the Lord, and bring the good news to one person this week.

intro: Theme: “I have no silver or gold, but what I have I give you.”
On Golden Friday, the first Friday after Pentecost, with St Helena: the power of the name of Jesus, the gold of love, and the treasure of those who leave everything.

sub: The hour of prayer.
The man at the gate.
“Look at us.”
q: then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the speechless sing for joy.
And by faith in his name, his name itself has made this man strong, whom you see and know
points.apply: Stop this week for one person you usually pass by; ask their name and listen to their story.

sub: Taken by the right hand.
Walking and leaping and praising God.
From outside the gate to inside the house of God.
q: The Lord lifts up those who are bowed down; the Lord loves the righteous.
Therefore God also highly exalted him and gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend
points.apply: Pray for a sick person in the name of Jesus each day this week, and visit them if you can.

sub: Tongues, prophecy, faith, all nothing without love.
Love is patient and kind.
Love that stops, looks and lifts.
q: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
Little children, let us love, not in word or speech, but in truth and action.
points.apply: Read 1 Corinthians 13:4–6 putting your own name in place of “love,” and choose the line that is least true of you to work on.

points.h: For God all things are possible
sub: The camel and the needle.
“We have left everything.”
St Helena: wealth spent for Christ.
q: Is anything too wonderful for the Lord?
For you know the generous act of our Lord Jesus Christ, that though he was rich, yet for your sakes he became poor, so that by his poverty you might become rich.
points.apply: Give one concrete gift to the poor or to the Church before Sunday, quietly, from what you would otherwise keep.

concl: On Golden Friday the Church shows her true gold: the name of Jesus, given in love.
Whether we have little or much, what is placed in Christ's hands lifts the lame, feeds the poor and builds the house of God.
2027-05-21.resolve: Look intently at the one at the gate, give what you have in the name of Jesus, and let love be the gold of your life.

intro: Theme: “You are a letter of Christ... written... with the Spirit of the living God.”
On Saturday after the Sunday of Pentecost, with St Rita: the letter written on hearts, the Spirit who gives life, and the oil that keeps the lamp burning.

sub: Not ink, but the Spirit.
Not stone, but hearts.
Read by all.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts
In the same way, let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
points.apply: At the end of each day this week ask: what did someone read about Christ in me today?

sub: The holy Law and its glory.
Command and strength.
“Give what you command.”
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you
And all of us, with unveiled faces, seeing the glory of the Lord as though reflected in a mirror, are being transformed into the same image from one degree of glory to another
points.apply: Name the commandment you find hardest to keep, and ask the Holy Spirit each morning this week for the strength to keep it.

sub: All of them slept.
Oil that cannot be borrowed.
St Rita's long night.
q: my soul waits for the Lord more than those who watch for the morning, more than those who watch for the morning.
Be dressed for action and have your lamps lit
points.apply: Do one work of mercy every day until next Saturday, and ask St Rita's prayers for one family you know in difficulty.

concl: The Spirit of Pentecost writes Christ on our hearts, so that our lives can be read by all.
Faith kept burning by prayer and mercy is the oil no one can lend us; St Rita kept hers through the longest night.
2027-05-22.resolve: Let the Spirit write on your heart, keep your lamp filled day by day, and be a letter in which others read Christ.

intro: Theme: “You are no longer strangers and aliens, but you are citizens with the saints and also members of the household of God.”
On Monday of the first week after Pentecost: the household of God, the stones fitted together by the Spirit, and the courage to confess Christ.

sub: From the gate to the table.
Citizens with the saints.
Built on the apostles, held by Christ the cornerstone.
q: for my house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.
like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, to be a holy priesthood, to offer spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Welcome one newcomer or one person who sits alone at church next Sunday.

sub: A house, not a heap.
The Spirit fits stone to stone.
Charity is the mortar.
q: My dwelling place shall be with them; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Do you not know that you are God's temple and that God's Spirit dwells in you?
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person in the family or the parish from whom you have drawn apart.

points.h: The glory that comes from God
sub: Believers who would not confess.
The fear of losing our place.
The Spirit makes witnesses.
q: Not to us, O Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven
points.apply: Choose one place where you usually stay silent about your faith and speak one simple word of witness there.

concl: The Spirit who came at Pentecost is building a house out of us, stone by stone, and Christ holds it together.
A living stone does not hide which house it belongs to.
2027-05-24.resolve: Let the Spirit fit you to your neighbour, and do not be ashamed to confess Christ before others.

intro: Theme: “We look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen; for what can be seen is temporary, but what cannot be seen is eternal.”
On Tuesday of the first week after Pentecost, with St Sophia, whose name means wisdom: the inner person renewed, the unseen that lasts, and the gifts we are to use until the Lord returns.

sub: The outer nature wastes away.
The inner person grows young.
The Spirit poured out at Pentecost.
q: He gives power to the faint, and strengthens the powerless.
I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory about to be revealed to us.
points.apply: Visit or call one elderly or sick person this week and pray with them.

points.h: Do business until I come back
sub: A pound for each servant.
The time between his going and his coming.
Trustworthy in a very small thing.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
Like good stewards of the manifold grace of God, serve one another with whatever gift each of you has received.
points.apply: Offer one gift you have, a skill, some time, a little money, to the parish or to a neighbour in need.

points.h: The wisdom that sees the unseen
sub: Sophia: the name means wisdom.
Weighing all on the scale of eternity.
Spending the visible to gain the invisible.
q: Therefore I prayed, and understanding was given me; I called on God, and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
If any of you is lacking in wisdom, ask God, who gives to all generously and ungrudgingly, and it will be given you.
points.apply: Each morning this week ask the Holy Spirit for the gift of wisdom before you begin your work.

concl: The body may grow weak, but the Spirit renews the inner person day by day and prepares a weight of glory.
The Lord has given us his gifts for the time until he returns: wisdom uses them, fear buries them.
2027-05-25.resolve: Look at what cannot be seen, and do not bury the pound the Lord has given you.

intro: Theme: “Lord, to whom can we go? You have the words of eternal life.”
On Wednesday of the first week after Pentecost, with St Philip Neri: the Twelve who stayed, the word that works in believers, and the joy of the Spirit.

points.h: Not a human word but God's word
sub: Received, not merely heard.
A word at work in believers.
Read with the Church's teaching and with humility.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty
Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the coming Sunday at home before you hear it in church.

points.h: Lord, to whom can we go?
sub: Many left; the Twelve stayed.
Believing in order to understand.
The bread of life on the altar.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me will never be hungry, and whoever believes in me will never be thirsty.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week and repeat Peter's words slowly.

points.h: St Philip Neri: the joy of the Spirit
sub: A heart set on fire at Pentecost.
Hours in the confessional, a room of prayer and music.
Humble, cheerful, loved by all.
q: for the joy of the Lord is your strength.
Rejoice in the Lord always; again I will say, Rejoice.
points.apply: Bring cheer to one person who is sad or lonely this week, and go to confession if you have been putting it off.

concl: Peter stayed because no other road leads to life; St Philip Neri stayed and found that the road was full of joy.
The word of God and the bread of life are given at one table, and both work in those who receive them.
2027-05-26.resolve: When it is hard, stay with Jesus, and let the joy of the Spirit be seen in you.

intro: Theme: “Daughter, your faith has made you well; go in peace.”
On Thursday of the first week after Pentecost: the things that are above, the life hidden with Christ in God, and the faith that touches him.

points.h: Seek the things that are above
sub: Christ seated at the right hand of God.
Not despising the earth, but setting the compass.
With him there while we are still here.
q: To you I lift up my eyes, O you who are enthroned in the heavens!
But our citizenship is in heaven, and it is from there that we are expecting a Savior, the Lord Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Begin each piece of work today with a short offering to Christ at the Father's right hand.

sub: Twelve years of sickness and shame.
The fringe of a faithful Israelite's cloak.
Power went out from him.
q: But for you who revere my name the sun of righteousness shall rise, with healing in its wings.
and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.
points.apply: At your next Holy Qurbono, come with a hidden need and receive the Lord with deliberate faith.

sub: He would not let her stay hidden.
A word that restored her dignity.
The peace that Christ gives.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you.
points.apply: Speak a word of welcome this week to someone who feels on the edge of the parish.

concl: Our life is hidden with Christ in God, and our hearts are turned to him above.
In the crowd at the altar, faith reaches out, touches him, and hears his word of peace.
2027-05-27.resolve: Set your heart on the things above, and come to the Holy Qurbono to touch Christ with faith.

intro: Theme: “She out of her poverty has put in everything she had, all she had to live on.”
On Friday of the first week after Pentecost, the day of the Cross: Timothy sent to strengthen the shaken, and the widow who gave her whole living.

sub: Paul gives up his best helper.
A pastor's anxious love.
Every Christian can be a Timothy.
q: Strengthen the weak hands, and make firm the feeble knees.
And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds
points.apply: Write or call one person this week who needs encouragement in faith.

points.h: So that no one would be shaken
sub: The honest cost of discipleship.
The tempter of discouragement.
Faith kept alive by companionship.
q: He alone is my rock and my salvation, my fortress; I shall not be shaken.
Indeed, all who want to live a godly life in Christ Jesus will be persecuted.
points.apply: Pray each day this week for Christians who suffer for their faith, naming one country where they are persecuted.

sub: Two small copper coins.
God measures by cost and trust.
The Lord who gave his whole life on the Cross.
q: For all things come from you, and of your own have we given you.
Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.
points.apply: Set aside your offering for the poor first, before other spending, as a sign that God comes first.

concl: The Church strengthens the shaken by sending its members to one another.
The widow's two coins point to the Cross, where the Lord gave everything.
2027-05-28.resolve: Encourage someone who is shaken, and give God not your leftovers but yourself.

intro: Theme: “Whoever does not carry the cross and follow me cannot be my disciple.”
On Saturday of the first week after Pentecost, the eve of Vocations Day, with St Theodosia: shepherds for every town, the virtues of God's steward, and the cross of every disciple.

sub: Titus left in Crete.
The apostles and those they appointed.
Where the bishop is, there let the people be.
q: I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.
tend the flock of God that is in your charge, exercising the oversight, not under compulsion but willingly
points.apply: Thank your parish priest this week, and pray for your bishop by name.

sub: A household that belongs to God.
Virtues learned first at home.
Families as the first seminary.
q: It is good for one to bear the yoke in youth
Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Keep the family evening prayer every day this week, and include a prayer for vocations.

sub: Christ loved above all, even above life.
The royal road of the holy Cross.
A young martyr who asked to be remembered.
q: Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of his faithful ones.
But they have conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, for they did not cling to life even in the face of death.
points.apply: Accept one daily cross this week without complaint, and offer it for those who suffer for their faith.

concl: The Church lives by the shepherds God gives her, and they grow from homes where Christ comes first.
Every vocation passes along the road of the Cross, and the martyrs show that it leads to life.
2027-05-29.resolve: Pray for vocations, love Christ above all, and carry your cross behind him.

intro: Theme: “And this is eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent.”
On Monday of the second week after Pentecost, the last day of the month of Mary: faith and love growing together, the knowledge that is eternal life, and the Mother who believed.

sub: Paul's thanksgiving.
Steadfast under persecution.
Justice left to God.
q: The righteous flourish like the palm tree, and grow like a cedar in Lebanon.
And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love for one another and for all
points.apply: Thank God today, by name, for three people in your parish whose faith has helped yours.

sub: The hour of glory is the hour of the Cross.
Knowing God, not only knowing about him.
The glory the Son had before the world.
q: but let those who boast boast in this, that they understand and know me, that I am the Lord
And we know that the Son of God has come and has given us understanding so that we may know him who is true
points.apply: Read one chapter of St John's Gospel slowly each day this week, asking to know Jesus more deeply.

sub: The month of Mary closes.
She knew her Son as no one else did.
Carrying Christ to others in haste.
q: The Lord, your God, is in your midst, a warrior who gives victory
And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.
points.apply: Pray one decade of the Rosary today, meditating on the Visitation, and visit someone who needs company.

concl: Eternal life begins now, in knowing the Father and the Son whom he sent, and it shows itself in growing love.
The holy Mother of God, who believed and carried Christ to others, teaches us that knowing.
2027-05-31.resolve: Seek to know God, not only to know about him, and let your faith and your love grow together.
